items.title: Accessibility basics
items.text: NativeHTMLKit builds a native accessibility tree from your HTML (AccessKit, exposed through AT-SPI on Linux and UI Automation on Windows). Screen readers see roles, names and states derived from your markup, so ordinary semantic HTML is the most important tool.

items.title: Checklist
items.text:
• Use real elements. <button> for actions, <a href> for links, <input>/<select>/<textarea> for input, headings in order, lists for lists, <table> with <th> for tables. A <div> with a click handler is neither focusable nor announced as a button.
  • Name every control. Use <label for="id"> (or wrap the control in <label>); add aria-label only where no visible label exists, such as a search field.
  • Announce status changes. Put status text in an element with role="status" (polite) or role="alert" (important), and update it with set_text. The UI libraries' alert component uses role="status".
  • Keep keyboard paths. Everything must work with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space. Forms submit with Enter; modal <dialog>s close with Escape. Move focus deliberately after actions (document.focus(id), Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus), as the notes tutorial does after adding a note.
  • Do not rely on colour alone. Pair colour with text or icons (the status board shows the state as text in a coloured pill).
  • Respect preferences. Style for prefers-color-scheme and prefers-reduced-motion; Style with the supported CSS shows how.
  • Give images text. Every <img>, including live bitmaps, needs a meaningful alt; keep values you draw in a chart available as HTML text too (Live bitmap charts).

items.title: Check what assistive technology sees
items.text:
The get_accessibility_tree document operation returns the tree the host exposes (roles, names, states, relations, bounds). The sign-up form test reads it to confirm that its fields are named "E-mail" and "Repeat password":

tree = doc.command("get_accessibility_tree")["tree"]
names = [(node["role"], node["name"]) for node in tree["nodes"] if node["name"]]

PowerShell: Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Document $doc -Operation get_accessibility_tree.

This is a quick structural check, not a substitute for testing with a screen reader (Orca on Linux, Narrator or NVDA on Windows).

items.title: Known limitations
items.text: Screen-reader coverage is still being qualified. Core 1.0.3 has a reported Orca issue with collapsed <select> announcements on Linux, and UI-library-specific screen-reader coverage is incomplete; see limitations.

items.title: Background work
items.text: Goal: run something slow (a computation, file processing, a network call of your own) without freezing the window, show progress, and allow cancelling.

items.title: Python SDK: a worker thread
items.text:
Event callbacks of one application run in order on one event worker. A slow callback delays every following event, so start a thread for the work and return. SDK calls are thread-safe: the worker may update the page directly.

examples/howto/python/prime_counter.py
"""Prime counter: run a long computation in a worker thread with progress and a Cancel button.

Teaches: keeping event callbacks short (they share one ordered event worker), starting a
threading.Thread for slow work, updating the page from that thread (SDK calls are thread-safe),
throttling progress updates, cooperative cancellation with threading.Event, and disabling controls
while a job runs.
Run:     python prime_counter.py
Guide:   docs/how-to/background-work.md
"""
import threading
import time

from nativehtmlkit import Application

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 15px sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 20px; background: #f4f6fa; color: #1d2433; }
  form { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; }
  input { width: 140px; padding: 6px; }
  button { padding: 6px 12px; }
  .track { height: 12px; background: #dde3ee; border-radius: 6px; margin: 16px 0 8px; }
  #bar { height: 12px; width: 0%; background: #2f6fd0; border-radius: 6px; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>Count primes</h1>
  <form id="job">
    <label for="limit">Up to</label>
    <input id="limit" type="number" min="10" max="50000000" step="1" value="2000000" required>
    <button id="start">Start</button>
    <button id="cancel" type="button" disabled>Cancel</button>
  </form>
  <div class="track"><div id="bar"></div></div>
  <p id="status" role="status">Ready.</p>
</body></html>"""


def count_primes(limit, cancelled, progress):
    """Sieve of Eratosthenes in chunks; calls progress(fraction) now and then."""
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    step = 0
    for n in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if cancelled.is_set():
            return None
        if sieve[n]:
            sieve[n * n::n] = bytes(len(range(n * n, limit + 1, n)))
        step += 1
        if step % 200 == 0:
            progress(n * n / limit)
    return sum(sieve)


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Prime counter") as app:
        window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Prime counter", width=520, height=320)
        doc = window.document
        job = {"cancel": None, "running": False}

        def set_running(running):
            if running:
                doc.set_attribute("start", "disabled", "")
                doc.remove_attribute("cancel", "disabled")
            else:
                doc.remove_attribute("start", "disabled")
                doc.set_attribute("cancel", "disabled", "")

        def worker(limit, cancelled):
            started = time.monotonic()
            last = [0.0]

            def progress(fraction):
                now = time.monotonic()
                if now - last[0] > 0.1:  # at most ten page updates per second
                    last[0] = now
                    doc.set_attribute("bar", "style", f"width: {fraction * 100:.0f}%")
                    doc.set_text("status", f"Working... {fraction:.0%}")

            try:
                result = count_primes(limit, cancelled, progress)
                if result is None:
                    doc.set_text("status", "Cancelled.")
                else:
                    doc.set_attribute("bar", "style", "width: 100%")
                    doc.set_text("status", f"Done: {result:,} primes up to {limit:,} "
                                           f"in {time.monotonic() - started:.2f} s.")
                set_running(False)
            except Exception as error:  # StaleDocumentError when the window closed mid-job
                print(f"Prime job stopped: {type(error).__name__}")
            finally:
                job["running"] = False

        def start(_event):
            if job["running"]:
                return  # one job at a time
            job["running"] = True
            limit = int(doc.get_value("limit"))
            job["cancel"] = threading.Event()
            set_running(True)
            doc.set_text("status", "Starting...")
            # daemon=True: a running job never keeps the process alive after the window closed.
            threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(limit, job["cancel"]), daemon=True).start()

        def cancel(_event):
            if job["cancel"] is not None:
                job["cancel"].set()

        doc.on("submit", start, element="job")
        doc.on("click", cancel, element="cancel")
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and Python SDK 0.1.2.

  • Throttle progress updates (here at most ten per second); each update is a message to the host.
  • Cancel cooperatively with a threading.Event that the work checks regularly.
  • Make worker threads daemon=True, and catch the stale-document error raised when the window closes while the job runs.
  • For SDK requests that may take long themselves (dialogs), use their wait=False form instead of a thread; see file dialogs. An asyncio adapter also exists (app.async_adapter()), documented in the Python SDK reference.

items.title: Python UI: set state from the worker
items.text:
State.set() may be called from any thread; the library schedules the page update on the UI's owner thread. ui.post(callable, *args) runs a function on that owner thread when you need ordering with other UI work.

examples/howto/python-ui/word_counter.py
"""Word counter: count words in a large text file in a worker thread and show progress with UI state.

Teaches: starting background work from a UI event, setting State from a worker thread (bindings
marshal the page update onto the UI owner thread), throttled progress, a Cancel button, and
avoiding computed() values whose dependencies change on several threads at once (a known
limitation in nativehtmlkit_ui 0.1.1).
Run:     python word_counter.py [FILE]   (without FILE it generates sample text in memory)
Guide:   docs/how-to/background-work.md
"""
import re
import sys
import threading
import time
from collections import Counter
from contextlib import nullcontext
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state

WORD = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]+(?:'[^\W\d_]+)?")


def sample_lines():
    words = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while native windows render html".split()
    for i in range(200_000):
        yield " ".join(words[(i + j) % len(words)] for j in range(9))


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Word counter") as app:
        source = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
        progress = state("Press Count to start.")
        top_words = state([])
        running = state(False)
        cancel = threading.Event()

        def work():
            counts, lines, done, last = Counter(), 0, 0, 0.0
            try:
                opened = source.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if source else nullcontext(sample_lines())
                with opened as stream:
                    total = max(1, source.stat().st_size) if source else 200_000
                    for line in stream:
                        if cancel.is_set():
                            progress.set("Cancelled.")
                            return
                        counts.update(word.lower() for word in WORD.findall(line))
                        lines += 1
                        done += len(line.encode("utf-8")) if source else 1
                        if time.monotonic() - last > 0.2:  # at most five updates per second
                            last = time.monotonic()
                            progress.set(f"{done / total:.0%} - {lines:,} lines")
                progress.set(f"Done: {sum(counts.values()):,} words, {len(counts):,} different, {lines:,} lines.")
                top_words.set([f"{word}: {count:,}" for word, count in counts.most_common(10)])
            except OSError as error:
                progress.set(f"Cannot read the file: {error.strerror}")
            finally:
                running.set(False)

        def start(_event):
            if running.value:
                return
            cancel.clear()
            running.set(True)
            top_words.set([])
            progress.set("Starting...")
            threading.Thread(target=work, name="word-count", daemon=True).start()

        ui = UI(title="Word counter", theme="daylight", density="regular", width=560, height=520)
        with ui.column():
            ui.heading("Word counter", level=1)
            ui.text(f"Source: {source.name if source else 'generated sample text'}", muted=True)
            with ui.container("form") as form:
                with ui.row():
                    ui.element("button", css_class="nhk-button nhk-primary", attrs={"type": "submit"}, text="Count")
                    ui.button("Cancel", variant="secondary", on_click=lambda _e: cancel.set(),
                              disabled=lambda: not running.value)
            ui.on(form, "submit", start)
            ui.alert(progress)
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("Most frequent words", level=2)
                ui.text_list(top_words)
        try:
            ui.mount(app)
            app.run()
        finally:
            cancel.set()
            ui.dispose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Known limitation in UI 0.1.1

A computed() value can race when several threads change its dependencies at the same time. Keep background updates to plain state() values, as in this example, or post them to the owner thread with ui.post(). See limitations.

items.title: PowerShell: Start-NativeHTMLKitTask
items.text:
PowerShell callbacks run on your script's runspace, so a slow command in a callback blocks the window. Start-NativeHTMLKitTask runs a script block in an isolated runspace and calls -OnCompleted or -OnFailed back on your runspace, during the event pump.

examples/howto/powershell/file-hash.ps1
# File hash: compute a file checksum in the background while the window stays responsive (PowerShell).
#
# Teaches: Start-NativeHTMLKitTask (an isolated runspace: pass plain data with -ArgumentList, never
#          SDK objects), -OnCompleted / -OnFailed callbacks that run on the owning runspace,
#          -TimeoutMilliseconds, Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask for Cancel, and enabling/disabling buttons.
# Run:     pwsh -File file-hash.ps1 [-Path FILE]  (Windows PowerShell 5.1: powershell.exe -File file-hash.ps1)
# Guide:   docs/how-to/background-work.md
param([string]$Path = '')
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'File hash'

$page = @'
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 18px; background: #f4f6fa; color: #1d2433; }
  form { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: 8px 10px; align-items: center; }
  input, select { padding: 6px; }
  .buttons { grid-column: 2; display: flex; gap: 8px; }
  button { padding: 6px 12px; }
  #hash { font: 13px monospace; word-break: break-all; background: white; padding: 8px; border-radius: 6px; min-height: 1.2em; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>File hash</h1>
  <form id="job">
    <label for="path">File</label><input id="path" required placeholder="Full path of a file">
    <label for="algorithm">Algorithm</label>
    <select id="algorithm"><option>SHA256</option><option>SHA384</option><option>SHA512</option><option>MD5</option></select>
    <div class="buttons"><button id="start">Compute</button><button id="cancel" type="button" disabled>Cancel</button></div>
  </form>
  <p id="status" role="status">Ready.</p>
  <div id="hash"></div>
</body></html>
'@

# Runs in its own runspace with only the arguments it is given.
$hashJob = {
    param([string]$File, [string]$Algorithm)
    (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $File -Algorithm $Algorithm).Hash
}

$job = [pscustomobject]@{ Task = $null; Started = $null }

function Set-Running([bool]$Running) {
    if ($Running) {
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element start -Name disabled -Value ''
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element cancel -Name disabled -Remove
    } else {
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element start -Name disabled -Remove
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute -Document $doc -Element cancel -Name disabled -Value ''
    }
}

try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'File hash' -Width 620 -Height 380
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html $page
    if ($Path) { Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue -Document $doc -Element path -Value ([IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Path)) }

    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type submit -Element job -Callback {
        param($eventObject)
        if ($null -ne $job.Task) { return }
        $file = (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element path).Trim()
        $algorithm = Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element algorithm
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $file -PathType Leaf)) {
            Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text 'That file does not exist.'
            return
        }
        Set-Running $true
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element hash -Text ''
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text "Computing $algorithm..."
        $job.Started = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
        $job.Task = Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -Application $app -ScriptBlock $hashJob -ArgumentList @($file, $algorithm) `
            -TimeoutMilliseconds 600000 -OnCompleted {
                param($result)
                $job.Task = $null
                Set-Running $false
                Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element hash -Text ([string]@($result)[0])
                Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ("Done in {0:N2} s." -f $job.Started.Elapsed.TotalSeconds)
            } -OnFailed {
                param($failure)
                $job.Task = $null
                Set-Running $false
                $text = if ($failure -is [OperationCanceledException]) { 'Cancelled.' } else { 'Failed: ' + $failure.Message }
                Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text $text
            }
    }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element cancel -Callback {
        param($eventObject)
        if ($null -ne $job.Task) { Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask -Task $job.Task }
    }
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}
  • The task script block sees only its arguments: no variables, functions or SDK objects from your script. Passing an application, window, document or bitmap object is refused. Return plain data.
  • -TimeoutMilliseconds and Stop-NativeHTMLKitTask request cancellation; -OnFailed then receives a TimeoutException or OperationCanceledException. A worker that ignores the request keeps running (and keeps its slot) until it ends.
  • At most 8 tasks per application (32 per process) run at once.
  • Receive-NativeHTMLKitTask -Wait waits for a task while still answering host messages.
  • For periodic refresh, start the next task from -OnCompleted, as in the dashboard tutorial.

items.title: CLI
items.text:
The CLI shows one window per command and blocks until the user decides. Run other work before or after it, or start the command in the background of your shell script (nativehtmlkit select ... &) and wait for it.

More background: Threading and callbacks.

items.title: Clipboard
items.text:
Goal: read and write plain text on the system clipboard.

Python (Application) PowerShell Read text clipboard_text() Get-NativeHTMLKitClipboard -Application $app Write text set_clipboard_text(text) Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard -Application $app -Text ...

Only text is supported. A request can fail, for example in headless test mode (RPC error -32001, "Clipboard requires a native event loop") or when the desktop refuses access, so always handle the error.

capabilities() / Get-NativeHTMLKitCapabilities tells you more in advance: features.clipboard_text.available is false when the host knows there is no clipboard (headless) and null on a desktop, where only the actual request can tell.

items.title: Example: a clipboard text tool
PowerShell
items.text: The process dashboard tutorial copies its table with Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard inside try/catch.

items.title: Cut, copy and paste inside text fields
items.text: Text fields support the usual keyboard shortcuts natively. To run an editing command from code, use document.edit("copy" | "cut" | "paste" | "selectAll" | "undo" | ..., element) (PowerShell Invoke-NativeHTMLKitEditCommand). Clipboard editing commands complete asynchronously: acceptance of the command does not mean the system transfer succeeded.

items.title: Distribute your app
items.text:
Goal: give your app to other people so that they can run it with one command.

The SDK packages and the CLI archive contain the native host for each supported platform, so a NativeHTMLKit app needs no separate runtime install: the user installs your app and its normal package dependencies.

items.title: Start from a generated project
items.text:
Both SDKs generate a small, runnable project with the HTML, CSS and code in separate files:

nativehtmlkit-new my-app --name "My App"     # app.py, index.html, style.css, pyproject.toml, app.toml
cd my-app && python app.py

New-NativeHTMLKitProject -Path ./my-app -Name 'My App'    # app.ps1, index.html, style.css, app.toml
pwsh -File ./my-app/app.ps1

Use -WindowsPowerShell to generate an app.toml that names powershell.exe. Both generated apps are run by this site's test harness against the released packages.

app.toml is optional. Day to day you run the script directly; a launcher or deployment can instead start the host explicitly with the manifest (nativehtmlkit-python-host run --app app.toml, Start-NativeHTMLKitHost -Manifest ./app.toml). Check the [backend] program line: the Python generator writes the absolute path of the interpreter that created the project.

items.title: Python
items.text:
• Declare the dependency: dependencies = ["nativehtmlkit>=0.1.2"] (and nativehtmlkit_ui>=0.1.1 if you use the UI library) in pyproject.toml. pip then picks the wheel for the user's platform, which includes the host.
  • Users on Linux need glibc 2.39 or newer for the released wheel; on older systems pip finds no compatible wheel. Do not ship the source distribution as a fallback: it contains no host.
  • Ship HTML, CSS, images and fonts as package data and locate them relative to your module (Path(__file__).parent), as the generated app.py does.
  • Give your app a stable identity: Application.start(name=..., app_id="org.example.MyApp"). The default id is derived from the script path, which changes when users install the app elsewhere.
  • instance="single" (the default) forwards a second launch to the running app; use "multiple" for tools that may run several times at once.

items.title: PowerShell
items.text:
• Publish a module or script whose manifest requires NativeHTMLKit (and NativeHTMLKit.UI if used), for example RequiredModules = @(@{ ModuleName = 'NativeHTMLKit'; ModuleVersion = '0.1.2' }). Install-Module then installs the SDK, which contains the hosts for Linux x64 and Windows x64.
  • Users start the app with pwsh -File app.ps1 (or powershell.exe -File app.ps1). Start-NativeHTMLKitScript must find the script file, so do not paste the code into an interactive prompt.
  • Set -AppId 'org.example.MyApp' on Start-NativeHTMLKitScript for a stable identity, and -Instance multiple if needed.

items.title: CLI scripts
items.text: Ship your script together with the instruction to install the CLI archive (or vendor the archive's folder next to your script and call it with an explicit path). Keep nativehtmlkit, nhk and nativehtmlkit-host in the same folder. Verify release archives with the published SHA256SUMS.

items.title: Before you ship
items.text:
• Run your app once on each target desktop with a real user session (KDE Plasma Wayland, Windows).
  • Add a headless smoke test to your CI: run the app with NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1, check that it reaches ready, then stop it. This site's scripts/test-examples.py is a complete, standard-library-only example.
  • Include the licence notices: the packages carry the host's LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and licenses/ files; keep them when you repackage.

items.title: Native file dialogs
items.text:
Goal: let the user choose a file or folder with the operating system's own dialog.

Dialog Python (Window) PowerShell Open one or more files open_files(multiple=..., title=..., directory=..., filters=[...]) Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -Kind OpenFiles [-Multiple $true] Save as save_file(file_name=..., title=..., filters=[...]) Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -Kind SaveFile [-FileName ...] Choose a folder choose_folder(title=..., directory=...) Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -Kind ChooseFolder

Every dialog returns {"cancelled": bool, "paths": [...]}; a cancelled dialog has cancelled true and no paths. Filters are {"name": "Text files", "extensions": ["txt", "md"]} (extensions without a dot; "*" for all files).

items.title: Python: do not block the event worker
items.text:
With the default wait=True the call blocks until the dialog closes, and all later events of the application wait with it. In an event callback, pass wait=False: you get a concurrent.futures.Future immediately, and its done-callback runs on a separate completion thread, where SDK calls are allowed. future.cancel() asks the host to close the dialog.

examples/howto/python/file_preview.py
"""Text file preview: pick a file with the native open dialog, preview it, save a copy elsewhere.

Teaches: Window.open_files() and Window.save_file() with wait=False (the event worker stays free
while the dialog is open), file-type filters, handling cancel (an empty result), and showing
untrusted file content safely with set_text().
Run:     python file_preview.py [FILE]      (FILE is shown at start, without a dialog)
Guide:   docs/how-to/file-dialogs.md
"""
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application, RpcError

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: #f4f6fa; color: #1d2433; }
  .bar { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; }
  button { padding: 6px 12px; }
  #name { font-weight: 600; }
  pre { background: white; border: 1px solid #d5dbe8; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px; height: 360px;
        overflow: auto; white-space: pre-wrap; }
  #status { color: #5a6578; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <div class="bar"><button id="open">Open...</button><button id="save" disabled>Save a copy...</button>
    <span id="name">No file</span></div>
  <pre id="content"></pre>
  <p id="status" role="status">Choose a text file to preview its first 200 lines.</p>
</body></html>"""

FILTERS = [{"name": "Text files", "extensions": ["txt", "md", "log", "csv", "json", "py", "ps1"]},
           {"name": "All files", "extensions": ["*"]}]


def main():
    with Application.start(name="File preview") as app:
        window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="File preview", width=760, height=560)
        doc = window.document
        current = {"path": None}

        def show(path):
            path = Path(path)
            try:
                with path.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream:
                    lines = [line for _, line in zip(range(200), stream)]
            except OSError as error:
                doc.set_text("status", f"Cannot read {path.name}: {error.strerror}")
                return
            current["path"] = path
            doc.set_text("name", path.name)
            doc.set_text("content", "".join(lines))  # text content: never interpreted as HTML
            doc.set_text("status", f"{path.stat().st_size:,} bytes; showing {len(lines)} lines")
            doc.remove_attribute("save", "disabled")

        def opened(future):
            # Runs on a completion thread once the dialog closes; SDK calls are allowed here.
            try:
                result = future.result()  # {"cancelled": bool, "paths": [...]}
            except RpcError as error:  # for example: no native dialogs in headless mode
                doc.set_text("status", f"The file dialog is not available: {error}")
                return
            if result["cancelled"] or not result["paths"]:
                doc.set_text("status", "Cancelled")
            else:
                show(result["paths"][0])

        def saved(future):
            try:
                result = future.result()  # the same shape: one path unless cancelled
            except RpcError as error:
                doc.set_text("status", f"The save dialog is not available: {error}")
                return
            if result["cancelled"] or not result["paths"]:
                doc.set_text("status", "Cancelled")
                return
            target = Path(result["paths"][0])
            try:
                shutil.copyfile(current["path"], target)
            except OSError as error:
                doc.set_text("status", f"Not saved: {error.strerror}")
                return
            doc.set_text("status", f"Saved a copy as {target.name}")

        doc.on("click", lambda _e: window.open_files(title="Open a text file", filters=FILTERS, wait=False)
               .add_done_callback(opened), element="open")
        doc.on("click", lambda _e: window.save_file(title="Save a copy", file_name=current["path"].name, wait=False)
               .add_done_callback(saved), element="save")
        if len(sys.argv) > 1:
            show(sys.argv[1])
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and Python SDK 0.1.2.

items.title: PowerShell: waiting inside a callback is fine
items.text:
Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog waits for the result, and while it waits the SDK keeps pumping host messages, so lifecycle requests are still answered. -NoWait returns a request object for Wait-NativeHTMLKitRpc / Stop-NativeHTMLKitRpc instead.

examples/howto/powershell/csv-viewer.ps1
# CSV viewer: choose a CSV file with the native open dialog and show it as an HTML table (PowerShell).
#
# Teaches: Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -Kind OpenFiles with -Filters, the result object
#          (cancelled, paths), waiting for a dialog inside a click callback (the SDK keeps pumping
#          host messages meanwhile), Import-Csv, and HtmlEncode for every cell.
# Run:     pwsh -File csv-viewer.ps1 [-Path data.csv]   (Windows PowerShell 5.1: powershell.exe -File csv-viewer.ps1)
# Guide:   docs/how-to/file-dialogs.md
param([string]$Path)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'CSV viewer'

$page = @'
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: #f4f6fa; color: #1d2433; }
  .bar { display: flex; gap: 10px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 10px; }
  button { padding: 6px 12px; }
  table { border-collapse: collapse; background: white; }
  th, td { border: 1px solid #d5dbe8; padding: 4px 8px; text-align: left; }
  th { background: #e9eef6; }
  #status { color: #5a6578; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <div class="bar"><button id="open">Open CSV...</button><strong id="name">No file</strong></div>
  <div id="table"></div>
  <p id="status" role="status">Choose a .csv file; the first 500 rows are shown.</p>
</body></html>
'@

function ConvertTo-HtmlText([string]$Text) { return [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($Text) }

function Show-Csv([string]$File) {
    try {
        $rows = @(Import-Csv -LiteralPath $File | Select-Object -First 500)
    } catch {
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ('Cannot read the file: ' + $_.Exception.Message)
        return
    }
    $columns = @()
    if ($rows.Count -gt 0) { $columns = @($rows[0].PSObject.Properties.Name) }
    $html = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
    [void]$html.Append('<table><thead><tr>')
    foreach ($column in $columns) { [void]$html.Append('<th>' + (ConvertTo-HtmlText $column) + '</th>') }
    [void]$html.Append('</tr></thead><tbody>')
    foreach ($row in $rows) {
        [void]$html.Append('<tr>')
        foreach ($column in $columns) { [void]$html.Append('<td>' + (ConvertTo-HtmlText $row.$column) + '</td>') }
        [void]$html.Append('</tr>')
    }
    [void]$html.Append('</tbody></table>')
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml -Document $doc -Element table -Html $html.ToString()
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element name -Text ([IO.Path]::GetFileName($File))
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ("{0} rows, {1} columns" -f $rows.Count, $columns.Count)
}

try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'CSV viewer' -Width 820 -Height 600
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html $page
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element open -Callback {
        param($eventObject)
        try {
            $result = Show-NativeHTMLKitFileDialog -Window $window -Kind OpenFiles -Title 'Open a CSV file' `
                -Filters @(@{ name = 'CSV files'; extensions = @('csv') }, @{ name = 'All files'; extensions = @('*') })
        } catch {
            # For example in headless test mode, where native dialogs are unavailable.
            Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ('The file dialog is not available: ' + $_.Exception.Message)
            return
        }
        if ($result.cancelled -or @($result.paths).Count -eq 0) {
            Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text 'Cancelled'
        } else {
            Show-Csv @($result.paths)[0]
        }
    }
    if ($Path) { Show-Csv ([IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Path)) }
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• The dialog is modal to the window you call it on.
  • Native dialogs are not available in headless test mode; the request fails with an RPC error (code -32001). Both examples show the error instead of crashing.
  • Treat file content as untrusted: the examples show it with set_text / HtmlEncode.
  • The UI libraries have no dialog component; call these SDK methods on ui.window (Python) or the window returned by Start-NHKUi (PowerShell).

items.title: Build and validate forms
items.text:
Goal: collect input with an HTML <form>, let the host check the usual constraints, add your own rules, and read the values.

The renderer implements HTML form behaviour natively: required, type="email", minlength/maxlength, min/max/step, pattern, :invalid styling, Enter-to-submit (implicit submission), <button> submitters and form reset. Your app sees the outcome as events.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Put labelled controls in a <form id="..."> and give each a name.
  2. Subscribe to submit on the form. It only arrives when every control is valid.
  3. For a rule HTML cannot express, set a custom validity message on input (set_custom_validity(id, message); an empty message clears it).
  4. Optionally subscribe to invalid (sent once per failing control on a submit attempt; it does not bubble) to show your own message. The host focuses the first failing control.
  5. Read the values with form_data(form_id) (ordered entries with name, value, kind; repeated names are kept) or get_value(id), then reset_form(form_id) if you want the initial values back.

items.title: Python example
PowerShell example
items.text:
The same form with cmdlets. set_custom_validity and get_validity have no dedicated cmdlet; Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Operation runs any documented document operation.

examples/howto/powershell/signup-form.ps1
# Sign-up form: native HTML validation plus a custom rule, then read the submitted values (PowerShell).
#
# Teaches: required/type/minlength constraints checked by the host, the set_custom_validity document
#          command (via Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand) for a rule HTML cannot express, the
#          "invalid" and "submit" events, Get-NativeHTMLKitFormData and Reset-NativeHTMLKitForm.
# Run:     pwsh -File signup-form.ps1        (Windows PowerShell 5.1: powershell.exe -File signup-form.ps1)
# Guide:   docs/how-to/forms.md
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Sign up'

$page = @'
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 15px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #f6f7fb; color: #1d2433; }
  main { max-width: 440px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 24px; }
  label { display: block; margin: 12px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 8px; border: 1px solid #9aa6bf; border-radius: 6px; }
  input:invalid { border-color: #c0392b; }
  button { margin-top: 16px; padding: 9px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: #2f6fd0; color: white; }
  #problem { color: #b03224; min-height: 1.2em; }
  #result { margin-top: 16px; padding: 12px; background: #e8f3ea; border-radius: 6px; }
  #result:empty { display: none; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>Create an account</h1>
  <form id="signup">
    <label for="email">E-mail</label>
    <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
    <label for="password">Password (at least 8 characters)</label>
    <input id="password" name="password" type="password" required minlength="8">
    <label for="confirm">Repeat password</label>
    <input id="confirm" name="confirm" type="password" required>
    <label for="plan">Plan</label>
    <select id="plan" name="plan"><option value="free">Free</option><option value="team">Team</option></select>
    <button id="create">Create account</button>
  </form>
  <p id="problem" role="alert"></p>
  <div id="result" role="status"></div>
</main></body></html>
'@

try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'Sign up' -Width 520 -Height 600
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html $page

    $checkPasswords = {
        param($eventObject)
        $same = (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element password) -ceq (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element confirm)
        $message = if ($same) { '' } else { 'The passwords do not match.' }
        $null = Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Document $doc -Operation set_custom_validity -Parameters @{ element = 'confirm'; message = $message }
    }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type input -Element password -Callback $checkPasswords
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type input -Element confirm -Callback $checkPasswords

    # "invalid" is sent once per failing control when a submit is attempted; it does not bubble.
    # The host focuses the first failing control, so only that one is reported.
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type invalid -Callback {
        param($eventObject)
        if ((Get-NativeHTMLKitFocusedElement -Document $doc).element -ne $eventObject.element) { return }
        $validity = Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Document $doc -Operation get_validity -Parameters @{ element = $eventObject.element }
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element problem -Text ("{0}: {1}" -f $eventObject.element, $validity.message)
    }

    # "submit" only arrives after every constraint, including the custom one, passed.
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type submit -Element signup -Callback {
        param($eventObject)
        $values = @{}
        foreach ($entry in @((Get-NativeHTMLKitFormData -Document $doc -Form signup).entries)) { $values[$entry.name] = $entry.value }
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element problem -Text ''
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element result -Text ("Welcome, {0}! Plan: {1}." -f $values.email, $values.plan)
        $null = Reset-NativeHTMLKitForm -Document $doc -Form signup
    }

    Set-NativeHTMLKitFocus -Document $doc -Element email
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• A type="number" field has a default step of 1, so 12.50 is invalid unless you set step="0.01" (or step="any"). The expenses tutorial uses a text field and its own parsing instead.
  • Validity details: validity(id) returns valid, the browser-style flags (valueMissing, typeMismatch, ...) and the localised message. check_validity(form_id) lists invalid controls without submitting.
  • Trigger a submit from code with request_submit(form_id); it validates first, exactly like the user pressing Enter.
  • Python UI: wrap controls in ui.container("form"), add a submit button with ui.element("button", attrs={"type": "submit"}, text=...), and ui.on(form, "submit", ...) (see the expenses tutorial). PowerShell UI has no form container; validate bound states with a computed value as in the settings tutorial.
  • CLI: nativehtmlkit form --html form.html shows trusted HTML containing <form id="nhk-form"> and prints the submitted entries as JSON; see the CLI reference.

items.title: Handle events
items.text: Goal: run your code when the user clicks, types, changes a selection, presses a key or submits a form.

items.title: Subscribe to an event
items.text:
Python: document.on(event_type, callback, element="id"). PowerShell: Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type <type> -Element <id> -Callback { param($eventObject) ... }.

  • With element, the callback runs for events whose target is that element or anything inside it (delegation). Without it, it runs for every event of that type in the document.
  • The callback receives one event object. Useful fields: type, element (id of the nearest element with an id), path (ids from the target up to the document), value and checked for form controls, key and code for keyboard events, button, x, y for pointer events, submitter for submit.
  • Notifications arrive after the host has handled the input natively. A callback cannot cancel a default action retroactively; register prevent_default(element, event) (Python) or Set-NativeHTMLKitPreventDefault (PowerShell) in advance instead.
  • focus and blur do not bubble; for delegation use focusin and focusout. invalid does not bubble either: subscribe without element or on the control itself.
  • A document accepts at most 256 subscriptions. Prefer one delegated handler on a container over one handler per row.

items.title: Example: an event inspector
items.text:
This tool logs every event the host delivers, with its fields. Keep it around for debugging your own pages.

examples/howto/python/event_inspector.py
"""Event inspector: see exactly which events the host delivers, and with which fields.

Teaches: Document.on() for several event types, delegation with element=..., the event dictionary
(type, element, path, value, checked, key, ...), unsubscribing, and rendering a bounded log safely
with insert_html() + html.escape() and Node.trim_children().
Run:     python event_inspector.py
Guide:   docs/how-to/handle-events.md
"""
import html
import time

from nativehtmlkit import Application

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #14181f; color: #e3e8f0; }
  main { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 300px 1fr; gap: 16px; padding: 16px; }
  section { background: #1d2330; border: 1px solid #2f3a4d; border-radius: 8px; padding: 12px; }
  label { display: block; margin-top: 10px; }
  input, select, textarea { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; margin-top: 4px; padding: 6px;
                            background: #10141b; color: #e3e8f0; border: 1px solid #3b475c; }
  input[type=checkbox] { width: auto; margin: 0 6px 0 0; padding: 0; vertical-align: middle; }
  button { margin-top: 10px; padding: 6px 12px; background: #2f3a4d; color: #e3e8f0;
           border: 1px solid #4a5870; border-radius: 4px; }
  ol { margin: 0; padding-left: 20px; font: 12px monospace; }
  li { padding: 2px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #262e3c; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <section id="controls">
    <h2>Try these</h2>
    <button id="hello">Click me</button>
    <label for="name">Text field</label><input id="name" placeholder="Type here">
    <label for="color">Select</label>
    <select id="color"><option>red</option><option>green</option><option>blue</option></select>
    <label><input id="agree" type="checkbox"> Checkbox</label>
    <label for="notes">Text area (press keys)</label><textarea id="notes" rows="3"></textarea>
    <button id="pause">Stop logging key presses</button>
  </section>
  <section>
    <h2>Events (newest first)</h2>
    <ol id="log"></ol>
  </section>
</main></body></html>"""

FIELDS = ("element", "path", "value", "checked", "key", "button")


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Event inspector") as app:
        window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Event inspector", width=900, height=560)
        doc = window.document
        log = doc.node("log")

        def record(event):
            details = ", ".join(f"{name}={event[name]!r}" for name in FIELDS if event.get(name) not in (None, "", []))
            line = f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} {event['type']}: {details}"
            doc.insert_html("log", f"<li>{html.escape(line)}</li>", position="afterbegin")
            log.trim_children(50, from_start=False)  # keep the newest 50 (the first 50 children)

        # Delegation: one subscription per type covers every control inside #controls. (focus and blur
        # do not bubble, so their bubbling twins focusin and focusout are used for delegation.)
        for kind in ("click", "input", "change", "focusin", "focusout"):
            doc.on(kind, record, element="controls")
        stop_keys = doc.on("keydown", record, element="notes")

        def pause(_event):
            stop_keys()  # the returned function unsubscribes
            doc.set_text("pause", "Key presses are no longer logged")
            doc.set_attribute("pause", "disabled", "")

        doc.on("click", pause, element="pause")
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and Python SDK 0.1.2.

  • doc.on() returns an unsubscribe function; stop_keys() removes the keydown handler.
  • Node.trim_children(50, from_start=False) keeps the first 50 log entries (newest first) and removes the rest.

items.title: Delegation pattern
items.text:
One handler on a list, decide by the clicked id. Excerpt from the notes tutorial (tested in full there):

def list_clicked(event):
    action, _, note_id = (event.get("element") or "").partition("-")   # "done-3" or "delete-3"
    ...
doc.on("click", list_clicked, element="notes")

In PowerShell, register one Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Element notes callback the same way and read $eventObject.element.

items.title: Where callbacks run
items.text:
• Python: all document and window events of an application run in order on one event worker thread. Keep callbacks short; a callback that waits (for example for a native dialog with wait=True) delays the following events. See Background work.
  • PowerShell: callbacks run on your script's runspace, inside Wait-NativeHTMLKit (or inside any SDK command that waits for the host). Variables that callbacks change should be properties of a shared object; see the dashboard tutorial.
  • UI libraries: pass on_click= / -OnClick to buttons; inputs, selects and checkboxes update their bound state for you. ui.on(element, "submit", callback) subscribes to other supported events on a UI element (click, input, change, keydown, submit, auxclick, contextmenu).
  • CLI: there are no per-event callbacks; the command's exit status and stdout are the result.

Details: Threading and callbacks.

items.title: HTML dialogs
items.text:
Goal: ask for confirmation or a small piece of input in an in-window <dialog>, without a native message box.

  • show_dialog(id) shows a <dialog> modally by default (the rest of the page becomes inert and focus moves into the dialog); show_dialog(id, modal=False) shows it non-modally. PowerShell: Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog -Element id [-Modal $false].
  • close_dialog(id, return_value) closes it and sets its return value. PowerShell: Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog -Element id -Close -ReturnValue ....
  • When a dialog closes, for any reason, it fires a close event. Read the return value with the get_dialog document command ({"open", "modal", "return_value"}). Escape closes a modal dialog with an empty return value, so treat anything except your "yes" value as "no".
  • The <form method="dialog"> shortcut of browsers is not used here: give the dialog's buttons ids and call close_dialog from their click handlers, or handle a form's submit inside the dialog yourself.
  • Popovers work the same way: show_popover, hide_popover, toggle_popover (PowerShell Show-NativeHTMLKitPopover -Action show|hide|toggle).

items.title: Example
PowerShell
items.text:
The PowerShell SDK gallery opens and closes a dialog and a popover with Show-NativeHTMLKitHtmlDialog and Show-NativeHTMLKitPopover. Read the return value with Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Operation get_dialog -Parameters @{ element = 'confirm' }.

The UI libraries have no dialog component; use these SDK calls on the UI's document.

items.title: Live bitmap charts
items.text:
Goal: show pixels you compute yourself (a chart, a plot, a preview) and update them many times per second.

A live bitmap is a fixed-size RGBA image that belongs to one document. You create it with an id, reference it from an <img src="ui4me-bitmap://ID">, and present complete frames.

Step Python PowerShell Create bitmap = document.create_bitmap("chart", width, height) $bitmap = New-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap -Document $doc -Id chart -Width w -Height h Show <img src="ui4me-bitmap://chart" width="w" height="h" alt="..."> same Draw a frame bitmap.present(rgba_bytes) (try_present does not block) Send-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap -Bitmap $bitmap -Pixels $bytes Release bitmap.close() Remove-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap -Bitmap $bitmap
  • A frame is exactly width * height * 4 bytes of straight-alpha RGBA8, row by row from the top left. Sizes are limited (up to 4096 x 4096).
  • present returns once the host has taken a snapshot of the frame, which naturally limits your frame rate to what the host can show.
  • Bitmaps are released automatically when their document is replaced or the window closes. Presenting to a released bitmap raises a stale-handle error.
  • Keep text labels in HTML next to the image: they stay sharp, selectable and readable by screen readers. Give the <img> a meaningful alt.

items.title: Python: a scrolling line chart
PowerShell: a chart driven by your own loop
items.text:
Instead of Wait-NativeHTMLKit -UntilShutdown, this script pumps events for up to 250 ms at a time and draws a frame in between. Per-pixel loops are slow in PowerShell, so the chart is small and updated four times per second.

examples/howto/powershell/live-chart.ps1
# Live chart: a scrolling bar chart of this process's working set, drawn into a live bitmap (PowerShell).
#
# Teaches: New-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap with <img src="ui4me-bitmap://ID">, filling a byte[] RGBA8
#          frame, Send-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap, and an application loop that pumps events with
#          Wait-NativeHTMLKit -TimeoutMilliseconds between frames instead of -UntilShutdown.
# Run:     pwsh -File live-chart.ps1        (Windows PowerShell 5.1: powershell.exe -File live-chart.ps1)
# Guide:   docs/how-to/live-bitmap-charts.md
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Live chart'

$width = 240; $height = 100
$page = @'
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: #0c1018; color: #dfe6f0; }
  img { display: block; border: 1px solid #2c3a50; border-radius: 6px; }
  p { margin: 8px 0; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>Working set of this script</h1>
  <img src="ui4me-bitmap://memory" width="240" height="100" alt="Bar chart of the working set over time">
  <p><span id="value">-</span> <label><input type="checkbox" id="paused"> Pause</label></p>
  <p id="frames">0 frames</p>
</body></html>
'@

$samples = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[double]
$state = [pscustomobject]@{ Paused = $false; Frames = 0 }

function New-ChartFrame {
    $pixels = New-Object 'byte[]' ($width * $height * 4)
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $pixels.Length; $i += 4) { $pixels[$i] = 16; $pixels[$i + 1] = 22; $pixels[$i + 2] = 32; $pixels[$i + 3] = 255 }
    $top = 1.0
    foreach ($value in $samples) { if ($value -gt $top) { $top = $value } }
    $offset = $width - $samples.Count
    for ($s = 0; $s -lt $samples.Count; $s++) {
        $bar = [int]([Math]::Round($samples[$s] / $top * ($height - 4)))
        $x = $offset + $s
        for ($y = $height - $bar; $y -lt $height; $y++) {
            $i = ($y * $width + $x) * 4
            $pixels[$i] = 90; $pixels[$i + 1] = 170; $pixels[$i + 2] = 255
        }
    }
    return ,$pixels
}

$bitmap = $null
try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'Live chart' -Width 300 -Height 300
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html $page
    $bitmap = New-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap -Document $doc -Id memory -Width $width -Height $height
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type change -Element paused -Callback {
        param($eventObject) $state.Paused = [bool]$eventObject.checked
    }
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app
    $clock = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
    # Our own loop: handle events for up to 250 ms, then draw the next frame. The diagnostic
    # report tells when the host has shut the application down (last window closed or quit).
    while ($true) {
        $null = Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -TimeoutMilliseconds 250
        if ((Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport -Application $app).Connection.ShutdownRequested) { break }
        if ($state.Paused -or $clock.ElapsedMilliseconds -lt 250) { continue }
        $clock.Restart()
        $megabytes = [System.Diagnostics.Process]::GetCurrentProcess().WorkingSet64 / 1MB
        $samples.Add($megabytes)
        if ($samples.Count -gt $width) { $samples.RemoveAt(0) }
        $null = Send-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap -Bitmap $bitmap -Pixels (New-ChartFrame)
        $state.Frames++
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element value -Text ("{0:N1} MB" -f $megabytes)
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element frames -Text "$($state.Frames) frames"
    }
} finally {
    if ($null -ne $bitmap) { Remove-NativeHTMLKitLiveBitmap -Bitmap $bitmap -Quiet }
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}
  • (Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport -Application $app).Connection.ShutdownRequested becomes true when the host shuts the app down; the loop then ends and finally releases everything.
  • To keep -UntilShutdown, schedule frames with background tasks instead (see Background work).

Bitmaps are not a video player: there is no audio and no codec. The UI libraries have no bitmap component; create the bitmap on the UI's document with the SDK.

items.title: Use multiple windows
items.text:
Goal: open more windows from one application, keep track of them, and close them together.

  • Every app.open_html(...) / New-NativeHTMLKitWindow creates another native window with its own document. Subscribe to events on that window's document, not the first one.
  • window.request_close() / Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow asks the host to close a window. The close can be vetoed by a policy set with window.on_before_close(callback) / Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeClose (return true to allow).
  • app.on_window_event(callback) / Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification -Method window.event reports close_requested, closed, resized, focused and other window events. When a window is closed its handles are retired by the SDK first.
  • The application ends when its last window closes. For that last window, Core 1.0.x sends no closed event: the application shutdown follows directly (your app.run() / Wait-NativeHTMLKit -UntilShutdown returns).
  • An app may open up to 16 windows by default (max_windows / -MaxWindows when starting).

items.title: Example: one viewer window per log source
PowerShell
items.text: The same building blocks: New-NativeHTMLKitWindow + Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml per window, Get-NativeHTMLKitWindowList, Close-NativeHTMLKitWindow, Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeClose, and Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification -Method window.event for window events. The PowerShell SDK gallery opens a second window from a button.

items.title: UI libraries
items.text: A UI object owns one window. Open further windows with the SDK next to it, or create and mount a second UI object.

items.title: Style with the supported CSS
items.text:
Goal: style your pages with confidence, knowing which CSS the renderer supports, and change styles at run time.

The host renders a documented desktop CSS profile (ui4me-desktop-1.0 in Core 1.0.3), not the whole web platform. Most everyday CSS works. The Core 1.0.3 profile reports, among others, flex and grid layout, calc(), color-mix(), light-dark(), oklch(), @media, @container, @layer, @supports, @font-face, @keyframes, animation, transition, :has() and ::backdrop as on; the examples on this site also rely on custom properties (var()), prefers-color-scheme and :invalid, which their tests check.

items.title: Ask the host instead of guessing
items.text:
The css_profile document operation lists the profile's features with a state each (on, off, filtered, unavailable). Run this explorer and type a feature name:

examples/howto/python/css_support.py
"""CSS support explorer: ask the running host which CSS features its renderer profile enables.

Teaches: the low-level Document.command("css_profile") operation, rendering a large table from data
with escaping, and a live "input" filter. Use it before relying on a CSS feature: the renderer
implements a documented desktop profile, not every browser feature.
Run:     python css_support.py
Guide:   docs/how-to/styling.md
"""
import html
from collections import Counter

from nativehtmlkit import Application

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; padding: 16px; background: #f4f6fa; color: #1d2433; }
  input { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 8px; margin: 8px 0; }
  table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }
  td, th { text-align: left; padding: 4px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #dde3ee; }
  td.state { font-weight: 600; }
  tr.on td.state { color: #1d6b34; }
  tr.off td.state, tr.unavailable td.state { color: #8a1f1f; }
  tr.filtered td.state { color: #7a5300; }
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>CSS profile <span id="version"></span></h1>
  <p id="summary"></p>
  <input id="filter" type="search" placeholder="Filter, for example grid or color-mix" aria-label="Filter features">
  <table><thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th>State</th></tr></thead><tbody id="rows"></tbody></table>
</body></html>"""


def main():
    with Application.start(name="CSS support") as app:
        window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="CSS support", width=640, height=720)
        doc = window.document
        profile = doc.command("css_profile")
        features = sorted(profile["features"], key=lambda f: f["id"])
        counts = Counter(f["state"] for f in features)
        doc.set_text("version", profile.get("version", ""))
        doc.set_text("summary", ", ".join(f"{count} {state}" for state, count in counts.most_common()))

        def render(_event=None):
            needle = doc.get_value("filter").strip().lower()
            rows = [f'<tr class="{html.escape(f["state"])}"><td>{html.escape(f["id"])}</td>'
                    f'<td class="state">{html.escape(f["state"])}</td></tr>'
                    for f in features if needle in f["id"].lower()]
            doc.replace_html("rows", "".join(rows) or '<tr><td colspan="2">No matching feature</td></tr>')

        doc.on("input", render, element="filter")
        render()
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and Python SDK 0.1.2.

In Core 1.0.3 the profile reports, for example, @page, @view-transition, @custom-media, zoom, shape-outside, line-clamp (the -webkit-line-clamp form is on) and initial-letter as off, @counter-style and ruby layout as unavailable, and ::part, ::slotted and :host as filtered. doc.command("explain", element=id) (Python) or Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Operation explain (PowerShell) helps when a rule does not apply as expected.

items.title: Switch themes at run time
Files, fonts and images
items.text:
• window.load_file(path) / Open-NativeHTMLKitFile loads an HTML file; relative stylesheet, image and font URLs resolve against its folder. For HTML strings, pass asset_root= / -AssetRoot to name that folder.
  • Remote (network) URLs are never loaded; ship assets with your app, or register in-memory resources with register_resources() / Register-NativeHTMLKitResources and reference them as ui4me-res:// URLs.
  • The host ships the Noto Sans font (see its licence files), so text renders even when you bring no fonts.

items.title: Other entry points
items.text:
• UI libraries: add CSS with UI(extra_css=...) / New-NHKUi -ExtraCss; see Theme the UI library.
  • CLI: --css FILE adds a trusted stylesheet to select, view and form windows.

items.title: Theme the UI library
items.text:
Goal: choose a look for a nativehtmlkit_ui / NativeHTMLKit.UI window and adjust it to your brand.

Setting Python PowerShell Values Theme UI(theme=...) New-NHKUi -Theme cobalt (dark, default), graphite (dark), daylight (light) Density UI(density=...) New-NHKUi -Density compact (default), regular, comfortable Extra CSS UI(extra_css=...) New-NHKUi -ExtraCss appended after the library stylesheet

Theme and density are fixed when the UI is built. To let users change them, store their choice and apply it on the next start, as the settings tutorial does.

items.title: Override the design tokens
items.text:
Each theme is a set of CSS custom properties on body.nhk-theme-<name>: --nhk-bg, --nhk-panel, --nhk-panel-2, --nhk-border, --nhk-text, --nhk-muted, --nhk-accent, --nhk-accent-strong, --nhk-accent-text, --nhk-danger, --nhk-focus, --nhk-radius. Densities set --nhk-control-h, --nhk-font, --nhk-gap and --nhk-pad on body.nhk-density-<name>. Because extra_css comes after the library stylesheet, a rule with the same selector wins.

examples/howto/python-ui/theme_preview.py
"""Theme preview: try the UI library's themes, densities and a custom accent colour.

Teaches: UI(theme=..., density=..., extra_css=...), overriding the library's CSS custom properties
(--nhk-accent and friends) for one theme, and the main components side by side.
Run:     python theme_preview.py [cobalt|graphite|daylight] [compact|regular|comfortable] [#RRGGBB]
Guide:   docs/how-to/theming-ui.md
"""
import re
import sys

from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state

THEMES = ("cobalt", "graphite", "daylight")
DENSITIES = ("compact", "regular", "comfortable")


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Theme preview", instance="multiple") as app:
        args = sys.argv[1:]
        theme = args[0] if len(args) > 0 and args[0] in THEMES else "cobalt"
        density = args[1] if len(args) > 1 and args[1] in DENSITIES else "compact"
        accent = args[2] if len(args) > 2 and re.fullmatch(r"#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}", args[2]) else None
        # extra_css is appended after the library stylesheet, so the same selector wins.
        extra = (f"body.nhk-theme-{theme} {{ --nhk-accent: {accent}; --nhk-accent-strong: {accent}; "
                 f"--nhk-focus: {accent}; }}") if accent else ""

        name = state("Ada")
        enabled = state(True)
        size = state("m")
        ui = UI(title=f"Theme preview: {theme}/{density}", theme=theme, density=density, extra_css=extra,
                width=720, height=560)
        with ui.column():
            ui.heading(f"{theme.title()} theme, {density} density", level=1)
            with ui.row():
                ui.badge("Badge")
                ui.badge(lambda: f"Hello {name.value}")
                ui.badge(f"accent {accent or 'default'}")
            with ui.grid():
                with ui.card():
                    ui.heading("Controls", level=2)
                    ui.input(name, label="Name")
                    ui.select(size, [("s", "Small"), ("m", "Medium"), ("l", "Large")], label="Size")
                    ui.checkbox(enabled, label="Enabled")
                with ui.card():
                    ui.heading("Buttons", level=2)
                    with ui.row():
                        ui.button("Primary")
                        ui.button("Secondary", variant="secondary")
                        ui.button("Danger", variant="danger")
                        ui.button("Quiet", variant="quiet")
                        ui.button("Disabled", disabled=True)
            ui.alert("Alerts use role=status, so screen readers announce changes.")
            ui.text("Muted text for secondary information.", muted=True)
        try:
            ui.mount(app)
            app.run()
        finally:
            ui.dispose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and Python SDK 0.1.2 + UI 0.1.1.

python theme_preview.py daylight comfortable "#8a2be2"

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Change tokens rather than restyling component classes; the token names are part of the 0.1 stylesheet and fewer rules break when the library changes.
  • Check contrast when you change --nhk-accent: --nhk-accent-text is the text colour on accent backgrounds (primary buttons).
  • Component markup is generated by the library; do not rely on generated element ids.

items.title: First checks
items.text: Symptom Check No window appears Run nativehtmlkit-python doctor (Python), nativehtmlkit doctor (CLI) or Get-NativeHTMLKitHostPath (PowerShell). Are you in an interactive desktop session (not SSH, not a service)? pip install finds no wheel (Linux) The released wheel needs glibc 2.39+ (ldd --version). "must run from a script file" Run a saved file: python app.py, pwsh -File app.ps1. Interactive prompts, python -c and piped stdin are refused. Something happens twice at start Code before Application.start() / Start-NativeHTMLKitScript runs in both processes. Move it after the call. A click does nothing Is the element id right, and is the subscription on the document of this window? Was the document replaced (old subscriptions are gone)? Use the event inspector. StaleDocumentError / NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException The window was closed or the document replaced; see Documents and stale handles. RPC error -32008 during shutdown The application is shutting down; requests are refused. Usually harmless in late callbacks. Clipboard or file dialog fails with -32001 Not available in this session, for example in headless mode. Handle the error. The window freezes while working A callback is doing slow work; see Background work. A CSS rule has no effect Check the feature with the CSS support explorer and explain.

items.text:
All entry points share the levels off, normal (default: critical problems only), debug and trace:

NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS=debug python app.py
nativehtmlkit-python --diagnostics trace run my_app:main
nativehtmlkit --diagnostics debug select < items.txt

$env:NATIVEHTMLKIT_DIAGNOSTICS = 'debug'; pwsh -File app.ps1
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'My App' -Diagnostics Trace

items.title: Counters and support bundles
items.text:
• Python: app.host_diagnostics() returns the host's counters (for example dropped_notifications); nativehtmlkit-python support bundle.zip exports a redacted local support bundle.
  • PowerShell: Get-NativeHTMLKitDiagnosticReport -Application $app returns session, queue-loss and callback-failure counters; Export-NativeHTMLKitSupportBundle -Path bundle.zip -Application $app writes a sanitized ZIP.
  • Both bundles stay on your machine (nothing is uploaded) and leave out form values, tokens, file paths and raw output. Review them before you attach one to a bug report.

items.title: Headless test mode
items.text: Set NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 (SDKs) or NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1 (CLI) to run the full protocol without a window, for CI and smoke tests. There is no pointer or keyboard input, no clipboard, no native file dialog and no external opening. Document commands still work, so a test can type into fields (replace_control_range), submit forms (request_submit) and read the page back (get_html); scripts/test-examples.py does exactly that.

items.title: Reporting a problem
items.text: Open an issue in the repository that owns the component (links in the Reference), with the versions (nativehtmlkit-python version, Get-Module NativeHTMLKit, nativehtmlkit --version), your OS and desktop, the smallest script that shows the problem, and diagnostics at debug level.

items.text:
Goal: change what the window shows (text, attributes, classes, whole fragments) without reloading the document.

Change Python Document PowerShell Replace text (never parsed as HTML) set_text(id, text) Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText Set or remove an attribute set_attribute(id, name, value), remove_attribute(id, name) Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentAttribute [-Remove] Add or remove a class add_class(id, name), remove_class(id, name) Set-NativeHTMLKitClass [-Remove] Replace or insert trusted HTML replace_html(id, html), insert_html(id, html, position=...) Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml [-Position] Remove an element remove(id) Remove-NativeHTMLKitElement Several changes as one transaction batch([{"op": ..., ...}, ...]) Invoke-NativeHTMLKitBatch Find elements by CSS selector query(selector) (ids), query_nodes(selector) (also elements without ids) Find-NativeHTMLKitElement, Get-NativeHTMLKitNodes Control values get_value/set_value, get_checked/set_checked, set_selected_values Get-/Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentValue, Get-/Set-NativeHTMLKitChecked, Set-NativeHTMLKitSelectedValues Replace the whole document window.load_html(html) Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml again

Any other documented document operation is available through document.command(op, **fields) (Python) or Invoke-NativeHTMLKitDocumentCommand -Operation (PowerShell).

items.title: Example: a status board
Rules
items.text:
• Untrusted text goes through set_text, or through html.escape() / [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode() before it becomes part of an HTML string. replace_html/insert_html parse their argument as HTML.
  • Replacing the document makes old handles stale. After load_html / Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml, event subscriptions, nodes and bitmaps of the previous document are gone; using them raises a stale-handle error. Prefer targeted updates. See Documents and stale handles.
  • Control values are live state. A value="..." attribute in your HTML is only the initial value; read what the user typed with get_value.
  • UI libraries: change a bound state/New-NHKUiState instead of calling these methods on elements the library manages.

items.title: What is tested, and how
items.text:
scripts/test-examples.py runs every Python and PowerShell example through its normal entry point (Application.start(), Start-NativeHTMLKitScript) against the released packages (Python SDK 0.1.2, UI 0.1.1, PowerShell SDK 0.1.2, PowerShell UI 0.1.1, each bundling Core 1.0.3), with the host in headless test mode (NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1). For each example it:

  1. waits until the app announced ready;
  2. runs a short scenario through public document commands: typing into fields (replace_control_range, which fires real input events), submitting forms (request_submit, which validates and fires real invalid/submit events), opening and closing HTML dialogs, closing windows, and reading the live page back (get_html, get_computed_style, get_accessibility_tree);
  3. requests an orderly quit and checks the exit status, that stderr has no traceback or callback failure, that files the app should write were written, and that no process of the run is left behind.

CLI scripts run with the released CLI 0.1.2 and NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1; the headless window never decides, so the scripts are checked with --timeout (exit status 124), their other options and their error paths. All .ps1 files are also checked for Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility (parser, PowerShell 7-only syntax, ASCII-only source).

python3 scripts/test-examples.py --python VENV/bin/python --pwsh pwsh \
    --psmodulepath DIR_WITH_THE_TWO_MODULES --cli DIR_WITH_nativehtmlkit
python3 scripts/test-examples.py --list          # show every case
python3 scripts/test-examples.py --only notes    # run a subset

Not covered by the automated run: real pointer and keyboard input (so click-only paths, such as a button that copies to the clipboard, are exercised only on a desktop), the clipboard, native file dialogs, rendering pixels on screen, and screen-reader behaviour. These are checked interactively on the target desktops before screenshots are published.

items.title: Frequently asked questions
items.text:
Can I use JavaScript? No. There is no JavaScript engine. All logic runs in your Python or PowerShell program, which receives events and updates the page. See why native.

Can a page load images or CSS from the internet? No. Network URLs are always denied. Use local files under the asset root, registered ui4me-res:// bundles or inline styles. Your program itself may use the network and then display the result.

Why does my script run twice? The first run is the launcher that starts the native host; the host runs your script again as its backend. Keep side effects below Application.start() / Start-NativeHTMLKitScript or inside main(). See lifecycle.

Why does a click handler wait while a file dialog is open (Python)? Events are delivered in order on one worker thread, and open_files() waits for the user by default. Use wait=False and a done-callback. See file dialogs.

Why do clipboard or file-dialog calls fail in CI? In headless test mode (NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1) there is no native event loop: clipboard and native dialogs fail with RPC error -32001. Catch the error and show a message, as the examples do.

Can I simulate clicks in headless tests? There is no synthetic input. You can drive documented document operations — for example request_submit fires the form's submit event and replace_control_range fires input — and read the DOM back with get_text, get_value or get_html. Real input needs an interactive desktop.

pip install nativehtmlkit fails or installs a package without the host on Linux. The released Linux wheel is manylinux_2_39_x86_64: it needs glibc 2.39 or newer. On older systems pip may fall back to the source package, which has no native host. Run nativehtmlkit-python doctor to check.

Does it work with Windows PowerShell 5.1? Yes, on Windows, for both the SDK and the UI module. Linux needs PowerShell 7.2 or newer.

Does it support macOS? Not in the current releases. Targets are Linux (KDE Plasma, Wayland) and Windows x64.

Which entry point should I use? See choosing an entry point. In short: a shell pipeline → CLI; quick reactive forms → UI library; everything else (dialogs, multiple windows, bitmaps, full DOM control) → the SDK, optionally mixed with the UI library.

Can I mix the UI library with SDK calls? Yes. The UI library is built on the public SDK; native dialogs, extra windows, clipboard and live bitmaps are SDK calls you make next to it.

Are the screenshots on this site real? Images marked as illustrations or placeholders are not captures. Real screenshots are added only after interactive verification on a native desktop.

How do I report a bug? Open an issue in the repository that owns the behaviour: rendering and native windows in Core, commands in the CLI, language APIs in Python or PowerShell, components in the UI library, and documentation in this site's repository. Include the versions and, if possible, a diagnostic report (see troubleshooting).

items.title: Glossary
items.text: App id A reverse-DNS identity such as org.example.Notes (app_id= in Python, -AppId in PowerShell). It identifies the application for single-instance forwarding. Without one, a stable id is derived from the script path. app.ready The message a backend sends when startup is finished (at least one window exists). Python's app.run() sends it; PowerShell uses Set-NativeHTMLKitReady (or Start-NHKUi). It must arrive before the startup deadline. app.shutdown The host's message that the application is ending: the last window closed or a quit was accepted. It implies that every window is closed — Core 1.0.x sends no closed event for the last window — and the SDKs retire all handles. Asset root The folder that relative stylesheet, image and font URLs resolve against, and outside of which local resources are refused. By default the folder of a loaded HTML file; set it with asset_root= / -AssetRoot. Backend Your Python or PowerShell process, started and supervised by the host, holding the application logic. See lifecycle. Before-close / before-quit policy A callback the host asks before closing a window (on_before_close, Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeClose) or quitting (on_before_quit, Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeQuit). Returning false vetoes it. Delegation Registering one event handler on a container id; it fires for events whose path contains that id. See documents and handles. Document The HTML page shown in a window. Loading new HTML replaces it atomically and makes the previous document handle stale. Generation The identity of one loaded document. Handles and node references belong to one generation. Headless / test mode NATIVEHTMLKIT_TEST_MODE=1 (SDKs) or NATIVEHTMLKIT_CLI_TEST_HEADLESS=1 (CLI): the host runs the full protocol without showing windows. No user input, clipboard, native file dialogs or external opening. Host The native Core executable nativehtmlkit-host, bundled with each SDK and the CLI. It owns windows, rendering, input and desktop services. Launcher The first run of your script (python app.py, pwsh -File app.ps1). It starts the host, waits, and exits with the host's status; the host then runs the script again as the backend. Live bitmap A bounded RGBA8 image surface that your code fills with pixels and presents to an <img src="ui4me-bitmap://ID">. Released with its document. Node reference An opaque, generation-bound handle for an element that may have no id, returned by query_nodes / Get-NativeHTMLKitNodes. Owner thread / owner runspace The thread (Python UI) or runspace (PowerShell, PowerShell UI) that is allowed to perform UI updates. See threading. Protocol v1 The local JSON-RPC wire contract between backends/CLI and the host; stable since Core 1.0.3. Pump In PowerShell, processing of host messages on your runspace by Wait-NativeHTMLKit and by every waiting SDK call. Stale handle A window, document, node, bitmap or subscription whose host object no longer exists or was replaced. Using it raises StaleDocumentError (Python) or NativeHTMLKit.StaleObjectException (PowerShell). State / computed The UI library's observable values (state(...), New-NHKUiState) and derived values (computed(...), New-NHKUiComputed) that bound components follow automatically. Supervisor The host's role towards the backend: it starts it, watches it, and ends it on shutdown or failure. Task In PowerShell, bounded background work started with Start-NativeHTMLKitTask in an isolated runspace; its completion callback runs on the owner runspace. ui4me-res://, ui4me-bitmap:// URL schemes for in-memory resource bundles registered from code (register_resources, Register-NativeHTMLKitResources) and for live bitmaps. The ui4me- spellings are the stable v1 names.
