items.title: Tutorial: a Git branch picker (CLI)
items.text:
You will write git-pick, a Bash script that lists your local Git branches in a native window, switches to the one you pick, and can delete merged branches in a multi-select list. It shows how to use nativehtmlkit select safely in scripts: input formats, output, exit statuses and timeouts.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and CLI 0.1.2.

Time: about 20 minutes. You need: Bash, Git, and the nativehtmlkit command on your PATH (CLI in five minutes). Final code: examples/tutorials/cli-branch-picker/git-pick.sh.

items.title: Step 1: pick a branch
items.text:
examples/tutorials/cli-branch-picker/step1-pick.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Branch picker tutorial, step 1: offer the local branches in a native list and report the choice.
#
# Teaches: piping lines into `nativehtmlkit select`, capturing stdout, and the exit statuses
#          0 (chosen), 2 (cancelled), 124 (--timeout expired) and anything else (error).
# Run:     bash step1-pick.sh [--timeout SECONDS]     (inside a Git work tree)
# Guide:   docs/tutorials/cli-branch-picker.md (step 1 of 2)
set -euo pipefail

status=0
choice=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ \
  | nativehtmlkit select --title "Pick a branch" "$@") || status=$?

case $status in
  0) echo "You chose: $choice" ;;
  2) echo "Cancelled" >&2 ;;
  124) echo "No choice made in time" >&2 ;;
  *) echo "nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" >&2 ;;
esac
exit "$status"

Run it inside any Git work tree: bash step1-pick.sh.

  • git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ prints one branch per line, which is the default lines input format.
  • nativehtmlkit select opens the window and blocks. On success it prints the chosen line and exits 0.
  • choice=$(...) || status=$? keeps set -e from ending the script when the user cancels: the exit status is captured instead.
  • "$@" passes extra options through, for example bash step1-pick.sh --timeout 30.

items.title: Step 2: a table, switching, and deleting merged branches
items.text:
examples/tutorials/cli-branch-picker/git-pick.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# git-pick: choose a local Git branch in a native window and switch to it (CLI tutorial final code).
#
# Teaches: feeding TSV to `nativehtmlkit select`, reading the selection from stdout, handling every
#          exit status (0 chosen, 2 cancelled, 124 timed out, anything else an error), multi-select
#          with --multi, and keeping the shell script safe with `set -euo pipefail`.
# Run:     bash git-pick.sh [--timeout SECONDS]                 switch to the chosen branch
#          bash git-pick.sh --delete-merged [--timeout SECONDS] delete chosen branches already merged
#          bash git-pick.sh --print                             show the table that would be offered
#          (inside a Git work tree; needs `nativehtmlkit` on PATH)
# Guide:   docs/tutorials/cli-branch-picker.md
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  sed -n '2,11p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
}

die() { echo "git-pick: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

mode=switch
select_options=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --timeout)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || die "--timeout needs a number of seconds"
      select_options+=(--timeout "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    --delete-merged) mode=delete; shift ;;
    --print) mode=print; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "git-pick: unknown option: $1 (try --help)" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
done

command -v nativehtmlkit >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "nativehtmlkit is not on PATH (see the CLI install guide)"
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "not inside a Git repository"
current=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD || echo "(detached HEAD)")

# One TSV row per branch, most recently committed first. The CLI treats a double quote as CSV/TSV
# quoting, so quotes in commit subjects are replaced by apostrophes.
branch_table() {
  printf 'branch\tupdated\tlast commit\n'
  git for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate \
    --format='%(refname:short)%09%(committerdate:relative)%09%(subject)' "$@" | tr '"' "'"
}

# Runs `nativehtmlkit select`, prints the chosen branch names (first column), returns its status.
pick() {
  local title=$1; shift
  local output status
  set +e
  output=$(nativehtmlkit select --input-format tsv --output-format lines --title "$title" \
    "${select_options[@]}" "$@")
  status=$?
  set -e
  case $status in
    0) printf '%s\n' "$output" | cut -f1 ;;
    2) echo "git-pick: cancelled; nothing changed" >&2 ;;
    124) echo "git-pick: no choice made in time; nothing changed" >&2 ;;
    *) echo "git-pick: nativehtmlkit select failed with exit status $status" >&2 ;;
  esac
  return $status
}

case $mode in
  print)
    branch_table refs/heads/
    ;;
  switch)
    branch=$(branch_table refs/heads/ | pick "Switch branch (current: $current)") || exit $?
    [ -n "$branch" ] || die "no branch selected"
    if [ "$branch" = "$current" ]; then
      echo "Already on $branch"
    else
      git switch --quiet -- "$branch"
      echo "Switched to $branch"
    fi
    ;;
  delete)
    if [ -z "$(git for-each-ref --merged HEAD --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/ | grep -vxF -- "$current" || true)" ]; then
      echo "No merged branches to delete"
      exit 0
    fi
    # Offer every merged branch except the one you are on (row 1 is the header).
    chosen=$(branch_table --merged HEAD refs/heads/ | awk -F'\t' -v current="$current" 'NR == 1 || $1 != current' \
      | pick "Delete merged branches" --multi) || exit $?
    while IFS= read -r branch; do
      if [ -n "$branch" ]; then
        git branch --quiet -d -- "$branch"
        echo "Deleted $branch"
      fi
    done <<< "$chosen"
    ;;
esac
  • branch_table prints TSV with a header row (branch, updated, last commit), and --input-format tsv shows it as a table with columns. The CLI treats " as CSV/TSV quoting, so quotes in commit subjects are replaced.
  • --output-format lines prints each selected row as its cells joined by tabs, without the header; cut -f1 keeps the branch name.
  • pick turns every exit status into a clear message and returns it unchanged, and || exit $? makes the script exit with the same status: 2 when cancelled, 124 when --timeout expired.
  • --delete-merged offers only branches merged into HEAD (minus the current one) and passes --multi, so the user can tick several rows. Each is deleted with git branch -d, which refuses anything not merged.
  • --print shows the table without opening a window, useful when you change the format.

Try it:

bash git-pick.sh                 # switch branch
bash git-pick.sh --timeout 20    # give up after 20 seconds (exit status 124)
bash git-pick.sh --delete-merged # tidy up

Make it a Git command by saving it as git-pick somewhere on your PATH and marking it executable; then git pick works.

  • Use --multi and --timeout.

items.title: Tutorial: a live process dashboard (PowerShell SDK)
items.text:
You will build Process Dashboard: a native window with a table of running processes that refreshes itself in the background, can be filtered and sorted, paused, and copied to the clipboard. It works the same on Linux (PowerShell 7) and Windows (PowerShell 7 or Windows PowerShell 5.1).

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and PowerShell SDK 0.1.2 on PowerShell 7.7.

Time: about 30 minutes. You need: the NativeHTMLKit module and the first window from PowerShell SDK in five minutes. Final code: examples/tutorials/powershell-process-dashboard/dashboard.ps1.

items.title: Step 1: a table from Get-Process
Step 2: filter and sort
Step 3: background refresh, pause and copy
items.text:
Calling Get-Process inside a callback blocks the window while it runs. The final version collects processes in a background task and refreshes every few seconds.

examples/tutorials/powershell-process-dashboard/dashboard.ps1
# Process dashboard: a live process monitor built with the NativeHTMLKit PowerShell SDK (tutorial final code).
#
# Teaches: collecting data in the background with Start-NativeHTMLKitTask (an isolated runspace that
#          gets plain data in and returns plain objects), updating the page in -OnCompleted on the
#          owning runspace, scheduling the next refresh, pausing with a checkbox, filtering a cached
#          snapshot, and copying the table to the clipboard with Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard.
# Run:     pwsh -File dashboard.ps1 [-RefreshSeconds 3]
#          (Windows PowerShell 5.1: powershell.exe -File dashboard.ps1)
# Guide:   docs/tutorials/powershell-process-dashboard.md (step 3 of 3)
param([ValidateRange(1, 3600)][int]$RefreshSeconds = 3)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Process Dashboard'

$page = @'
<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 14px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #11161f; color: #e6ebf3; }
  main { padding: 18px 22px; }
  header { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; }
  h1 { font-size: 20px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
  #status { color: #9fb0c8; }
  form { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 10px; }
  input, select { background: #1b2331; color: #e6ebf3; border: 1px solid #3a475c; border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px; }
  #filter { flex: 1; }
  button { background: #3574c6; color: white; border: 0; border-radius: 5px; padding: 6px 12px; }
  table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }
  th, td { text-align: left; padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #2a3445; }
  th { color: #9fb0c8; font-weight: 600; }
  td.num, th.num { text-align: right; }
  #summary { color: #9fb0c8; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <header><h1>Processes</h1><span id="status" role="status">Collecting...</span></header>
  <form id="view-form">
    <input id="filter" type="search" placeholder="Filter by name" aria-label="Filter by name">
    <select id="sort" aria-label="Sort by">
      <option value="memory">Memory</option><option value="cpu">CPU time</option><option value="name">Name</option>
    </select>
    <label><input type="checkbox" id="paused"> Pause</label>
    <button id="copy" type="button">Copy table</button>
  </form>
  <p id="summary"></p>
  <table>
    <thead><tr><th>Name</th><th class="num">Id</th><th class="num">Memory (MB)</th><th class="num">CPU (s)</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody id="rows"></tbody>
  </table>
</main></body></html>
'@

# Runs in a separate runspace: no access to $app, $doc or this script's variables and functions.
$collect = {
    param([int]$DelayMilliseconds)
    if ($DelayMilliseconds -gt 0) { Start-Sleep -Milliseconds $DelayMilliseconds }
    Get-Process | ForEach-Object {
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $_.ProcessName; Id = $_.Id
            MemoryMB = [Math]::Round($_.WorkingSet64 / 1MB, 1); Cpu = [Math]::Round([double]$_.CPU, 1) }
    }
}

# Everything the callbacks change lives in one object, so they never need to assign script variables.
$view = [pscustomobject]@{ Rows = @(); Refreshes = 0; Task = $null; Shown = @() }

function ConvertTo-HtmlText([string]$Text) { return [System.Net.WebUtility]::HtmlEncode($Text) }

function Update-View {
    $filter = (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element filter).Trim()
    $shown = @($view.Rows | Where-Object { $filter -eq '' -or $_.Name.IndexOf($filter, [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) -ge 0 })
    $sorted = switch (Get-NativeHTMLKitValue -Document $doc -Element sort) {
        'cpu'  { $shown | Sort-Object Cpu -Descending }
        'name' { $shown | Sort-Object Name }
        default { $shown | Sort-Object MemoryMB -Descending }
    }
    $view.Shown = @($sorted | Select-Object -First 25)
    $html = @($view.Shown | ForEach-Object {
        '<tr><td>{0}</td><td class="num">{1}</td><td class="num">{2:N1}</td><td class="num">{3:N1}</td></tr>' -f `
            (ConvertTo-HtmlText $_.Name), $_.Id, $_.MemoryMB, $_.Cpu
    }) -join ''
    $total = ($view.Rows | Measure-Object MemoryMB -Sum).Sum
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentHtml -Document $doc -Element rows -Html $html
    Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element summary -Text ("Showing {0} of {1} processes, {2:N0} MB in total" -f $view.Shown.Count, $view.Rows.Count, $total)
}

function Start-Refresh([int]$DelayMilliseconds) {
    $view.Task = Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -Application $app -ScriptBlock $collect -ArgumentList @($DelayMilliseconds) -OnCompleted {
        param($rows)
        $view.Task = $null
        $view.Rows = @($rows)
        $view.Refreshes++
        Update-View
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ("Updated {0:HH:mm:ss} (refresh #{1})" -f (Get-Date), $view.Refreshes)
        if (-not (Get-NativeHTMLKitChecked -Document $doc -Element paused)) { Start-Refresh ($RefreshSeconds * 1000) }
    } -OnFailed {
        param($failure)
        $view.Task = $null
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text ('Refresh failed: ' + $failure.Message)
    }
}

try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'Process Dashboard' -Width 760 -Height 640
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html $page
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type input -Element filter -Callback { param($eventObject) Update-View }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type change -Element sort -Callback { param($eventObject) Update-View }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type submit -Element 'view-form' -Callback { param($eventObject) Update-View }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type change -Element paused -Callback {
        param($eventObject)
        if ([bool]$eventObject.checked) {
            Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text 'Paused'
        } elseif ($null -eq $view.Task) {
            Start-Refresh 0
        }
    }
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element copy -Callback {
        param($eventObject)
        $lines = @("Name`tId`tMemoryMB`tCpu") + @($view.Shown | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)`t$($_.Id)`t$($_.MemoryMB)`t$($_.Cpu)" })
        try {
            Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard -Application $app -Text ($lines -join [Environment]::NewLine)
            Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text "Copied $($view.Shown.Count) rows"
        } catch {
            Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text 'The clipboard is not available in this session'
        }
    }
    Start-Refresh 0
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}
  • Start-NativeHTMLKitTask -ScriptBlock $collect -ArgumentList @($delay) runs $collect in a separate runspace. It cannot see $app, $doc or your functions, and it must not receive SDK objects; pass plain data in and return plain objects (here [pscustomobject] rows).
  • -OnCompleted { param($rows) ... } runs back on the main runspace, during Wait-NativeHTMLKit, where it is safe to update the page. It stores the rows, re-renders and starts the next task: a self-scheduling timer without blocking the window.
  • -OnFailed receives the exception if the task throws, times out or is stopped.
  • Everything the callbacks change lives in one object, $view. Assigning $x = ... inside a script block would only create a local variable; setting $view.Rows changes the shared object.
  • The pause checkbox reads $eventObject.checked from the change event. Unpausing starts a new refresh immediately if none is pending.
  • Copy table uses Set-NativeHTMLKitClipboard inside try/catch: some sessions (for example headless test runs) have no clipboard.
  • -RefreshSeconds is a normal script parameter: pwsh -File dashboard.ps1 -RefreshSeconds 10. The host re-runs the script with the same arguments.
  • Close-NativeHTMLKit in finally also requests cancellation of a task that is still sleeping; no callback runs after it.

items.title: What you learned
items.text:
• Render tables from objects with encoded values; subscribe to input, change and submit.
  • Keep slow work off the event loop with Start-NativeHTMLKitTask, and update the page in -OnCompleted.
  • Share state between callbacks through one object; pass parameters through the re-executed script.

items.title: Tutorial: a settings editor (PowerShell UI)
items.text:
You will build Settings, a small editor for a JSON settings file with NativeHTMLKit.UI: bound inputs, live validation, an "Unsaved changes" badge, Save and Revert buttons, and a theme the app itself uses on the next start.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and PowerShell SDK 0.1.2 + UI 0.1.1 on PowerShell 7.7.

Time: about 25 minutes. You need: NativeHTMLKit.UI installed and the counter from PowerShell UI in five minutes working. Final code: examples/tutorials/powershell-ui-settings/settings.ps1.

items.title: Step 1: a form bound to state
items.text:
examples/tutorials/powershell-ui-settings/step1-form.ps1
# Settings editor tutorial, step 1: a form whose controls are bound to UI state.
#
# Teaches: New-NHKUi, New-NHKUiState, two-way Add-NHKUiInput / Add-NHKUiSelect / Add-NHKUiCheckbox,
#          New-NHKUiComputed with explicit -DependsOn, Add-NHKUiText -Bind, Start-NHKUi / Stop-NHKUi.
# Run:     pwsh -File step1-form.ps1        (Windows PowerShell 5.1: powershell.exe -File step1-form.ps1)
# Guide:   docs/tutorials/powershell-ui-settings.md (step 1 of 2)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Settings'

$name = New-NHKUiState -Value 'Ada'
$email = New-NHKUiState -Value 'ada@example.org'
$theme = New-NHKUiState -Value 'cobalt'
$notify = New-NHKUiState -Value $true
$summary = New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @($name, $email, $theme, $notify) -Data @{ Name = $name; Email = $email; Theme = $theme; Notify = $notify } -Compute {
    param($s)
    $mail = if ($s.Notify.Value) { 'with e-mail notifications' } else { 'without notifications' }
    "$($s.Name.Value) <$($s.Email.Value)>, $($s.Theme.Value) theme, $mail"
}

$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Settings' -Theme cobalt -Density regular -Width 560 -Height 520
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
    $null = Add-NHKUiHeading -UI $ui -Text 'Settings' -Level 1
    $null = Add-NHKUiCard -UI $ui -Content {
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $name -Label 'Display name'
        $null = Add-NHKUiInput -UI $ui -Bind $email -Label 'E-mail' -Type email
        $null = Add-NHKUiSelect -UI $ui -Bind $theme -Label 'Theme' -Options @(
            @{ Value = 'cobalt'; Label = 'Cobalt' }, @{ Value = 'graphite'; Label = 'Graphite' }, @{ Value = 'daylight'; Label = 'Daylight' })
        $null = Add-NHKUiCheckbox -UI $ui -Bind $notify -Label 'Send me e-mail notifications'
    }
    $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Bind $summary -Muted
}

try {
    $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
    Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
    $summary.Dispose()
    Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

Run pwsh -File step1-form.ps1 and edit the fields: the summary below follows every change.

  • Each New-NHKUiState holds one setting. Add-NHKUiInput -Bind $name is two-way; -Type email gives an e-mail field.
  • Add-NHKUiSelect -Options takes hashtables with Value and Label. Add-NHKUiCheckbox binds a Boolean.
  • New-NHKUiComputed -DependsOn @(...) lists its dependencies explicitly (PowerShell has no automatic dependency tracking), and receives -Data as its parameter.
  • The summary contains < and > around the e-mail address; Add-NHKUiText always encodes text, so this is safe.

items.title: Tutorial: a notes app with persistence (Python SDK)
items.text:
You will build Notes: a window where you add short notes, mark them done, delete them, filter them, and find them again the next time you start the app. Along the way you learn the core pattern of every NativeHTMLKit SDK app: keep the data in Python, render it into the page, react to events.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and Python SDK 0.1.2.

Time: about 30 minutes. You need: the Python SDK installed and a first window working (Python SDK in five minutes). Final code: examples/tutorials/python-notes/notes.py.

items.title: Step 1: a window that renders Python data
items.text:
Start with a page that has an empty <ul id="notes">, and fill it from a Python list.

examples/tutorials/python-notes/step1_window.py
"""Notes tutorial, step 1: open a native window and render a list from Python data.

Teaches: Application.start(), open_html(), building HTML from data with html.escape(), app.run().
Run:     python step1_window.py
Guide:   docs/tutorials/python-notes.md (step 1 of 4)
"""
import html

from nativehtmlkit import Application

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 15px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #f4f6fb; color: #1d2433; }
  main { padding: 20px 24px; }
  h1 { font-size: 22px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
  ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }
  li { background: white; border: 1px solid #d5dbe8; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; margin: 6px 0; }
  .done { color: #7a8396; text-decoration: line-through; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>Notes</h1>
  <ul id="notes"></ul>
</main></body></html>"""

SAMPLE_NOTES = [
    {"id": 1, "text": "Read the NativeHTMLKit tutorial", "done": True},
    {"id": 2, "text": "Build a notes app", "done": False},
]


def render_note(note):
    css = "note done" if note["done"] else "note"
    return f'<li class="{css}" id="note-{note["id"]}">{html.escape(note["text"])}</li>'


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Notes") as app:
        window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Notes", width=520, height=600)
        window.document.replace_html("notes", "".join(render_note(n) for n in SAMPLE_NOTES))
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run it with python step1_window.py. Things to notice:

  • The page is an ordinary HTML string with a <style> block. The renderer supports a large, documented CSS subset (flexbox, grid, custom properties and more; see Style with the supported CSS), but no JavaScript.
  • render_note() turns one note into HTML. Every piece of user text goes through html.escape() before it becomes markup. Later, notes come from the keyboard; without escaping, a note like <b> would change your page.
  • replace_html("notes", ...) replaces the children of the element with id notes. Ids are how Python points at parts of the page.
  • Everything happens inside main() after Application.start(), because the host runs this file a second time as its backend (why).

items.title: Step 2: add notes with a form
items.text:
A <form> gives you validation and keyboard behaviour for free: pressing Enter in the field submits it, and required stops empty submissions before your code sees them.

examples/tutorials/python-notes/step2_add.py
"""Notes tutorial, step 2: add notes with a form.

Teaches: an HTML <form> with a required field, the "submit" event, reading a control with
get_value(), appending escaped HTML with insert_html(), clearing and focusing the field.
Run:     python step2_add.py
Guide:   docs/tutorials/python-notes.md (step 2 of 4)
"""
import html

from nativehtmlkit import Application

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 15px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #f4f6fb; color: #1d2433; }
  main { padding: 20px 24px; }
  h1 { font-size: 22px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
  form { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 12px; }
  input { flex: 1; padding: 8px; border: 1px solid #9aa6bf; border-radius: 6px; }
  button { padding: 8px 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: #2f6fd0; color: white; }
  ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }
  li { background: white; border: 1px solid #d5dbe8; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; margin: 6px 0; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>Notes</h1>
  <form id="add-form">
    <input id="new-note" name="text" required maxlength="200" placeholder="What do you need to remember?"
           aria-label="New note">
    <button id="add">Add</button>
  </form>
  <ul id="notes"></ul>
  <p id="summary">0 notes</p>
</main></body></html>"""


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Notes") as app:
        window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Notes", width=520, height=600)
        doc = window.document
        notes = []

        def add_note(_event):
            # The form only submits when its "required" field is filled in.
            text = doc.get_value("new-note").strip()
            if not text:
                return
            notes.append(text)
            doc.insert_html("notes", f"<li>{html.escape(text)}</li>")  # never insert raw user text
            doc.set_text("summary", f"{len(notes)} notes")
            doc.set_value("new-note", "")
            doc.focus("new-note")

        doc.on("submit", add_note, element="add-form")
        doc.focus("new-note")
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
  • doc.on("submit", add_note, element="add-form") runs add_note when the form is submitted, by Enter or by the button. The host validates first: with an empty field there is no submit event at all.
  • Event callbacks get one argument, the event dictionary. This handler does not need it, so it is named _event.
  • get_value("new-note") reads what the user typed; insert_html(..., "<li>...</li>") appends to the list (position beforeend by default).
  • set_value("new-note", "") clears the field and focus("new-note") puts the cursor back, so you can type the next note immediately.

items.title: Step 3: done and delete buttons
items.text:
Each note now gets two buttons. Instead of subscribing once per button (and again whenever the list changes), subscribe once on the list and look at which element was clicked.

examples/tutorials/python-notes/step3_actions.py
"""Notes tutorial, step 3: mark notes done and delete them.

Teaches: keeping the data model in Python and re-rendering the list from it, one delegated "click"
handler for many buttons (event["element"] is the id of the clicked element), stable element ids.
Run:     python step3_actions.py
Guide:   docs/tutorials/python-notes.md (step 3 of 4)
"""
import html

from nativehtmlkit import Application

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 15px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #f4f6fb; color: #1d2433; }
  main { padding: 20px 24px; }
  h1 { font-size: 22px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
  form { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 12px; }
  input { flex: 1; padding: 8px; border: 1px solid #9aa6bf; border-radius: 6px; }
  button { padding: 8px 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: #2f6fd0; color: white; }
  ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }
  li { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: white; border: 1px solid #d5dbe8;
       border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; margin: 6px 0; }
  li .text { flex: 1; }
  li.done .text { color: #7a8396; text-decoration: line-through; }
  li button { padding: 4px 10px; background: #e3e8f3; color: #1d2433; }
  li button.danger { background: #f6dede; color: #8a1f1f; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>Notes</h1>
  <form id="add-form">
    <input id="new-note" name="text" required maxlength="200" placeholder="What do you need to remember?"
           aria-label="New note">
    <button id="add">Add</button>
  </form>
  <ul id="notes"></ul>
  <p id="summary"></p>
</main></body></html>"""


def render_note(note):
    css = "done" if note["done"] else ""
    label = "Undo" if note["done"] else "Done"
    return (f'<li class="{css}" id="note-{note["id"]}">'
            f'<span class="text">{html.escape(note["text"])}</span>'
            f'<button id="done-{note["id"]}">{label}</button>'
            f'<button id="delete-{note["id"]}" class="danger">Delete</button></li>')


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Notes") as app:
        window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Notes", width=520, height=600)
        doc = window.document
        notes = []

        def refresh():
            doc.replace_html("notes", "".join(render_note(n) for n in notes))
            remaining = sum(1 for n in notes if not n["done"])
            doc.set_text("summary", f"{len(notes)} notes, {remaining} open")

        def add_note(_event):
            text = doc.get_value("new-note").strip()
            if not text:
                return
            next_id = max((n["id"] for n in notes), default=0) + 1
            notes.append({"id": next_id, "text": text, "done": False})
            refresh()
            doc.set_value("new-note", "")
            doc.focus("new-note")

        def list_clicked(event):
            # One handler for every button in the list: "done-3" or "delete-3".
            action, _, note_id = (event.get("element") or "").partition("-")
            note = next((n for n in notes if str(n["id"]) == note_id), None)
            if note is None:
                return
            if action == "done":
                note["done"] = not note["done"]
            elif action == "delete":
                notes.remove(note)
            refresh()

        doc.on("submit", add_note, element="add-form")
        doc.on("click", list_clicked, element="notes")
        refresh()
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
  • Notes are dictionaries with a stable id. Button ids encode the action and the note: done-3, delete-3.
  • doc.on("click", list_clicked, element="notes") is a delegated handler: it fires for clicks anywhere inside #notes. event["element"] is the id of the nearest element with an id that was clicked, and event["path"] lists the ids from there up to the document.
  • The handler changes the Python list, then refresh() renders the whole list again. For lists of this size, re-rendering is simple and fast, and the model in Python stays the single source of truth.
  • Clicking the note text itself yields note-3, which the handler ignores.

items.title: Step 4: save to a file and filter
items.text:
The final version keeps notes in a JSON file, loads them at start, and adds a live filter.

examples/tutorials/python-notes/notes.py
"""Notes: a small persistent notes app built with the NativeHTMLKit Python SDK (tutorial final code).

Teaches: a form with validation and the "submit" event, a delegated "click" handler, a live
"input" filter, re-rendering escaped HTML from a Python model, and saving the model to a JSON file
with an atomic replace.
Run:     python notes.py [NOTES_FILE]
         (default file: .nativehtmlkit-notes.json in your home directory)
Guide:   docs/tutorials/python-notes.md (step 4 of 4)
"""
import html
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application

PAGE = """<!doctype html>
<html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>
  body { font: 15px sans-serif; margin: 0; background: #f4f6fb; color: #1d2433; }
  main { padding: 20px 24px; }
  h1 { font-size: 22px; margin: 0 0 12px; }
  form { display: flex; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 12px; }
  input { padding: 8px; border: 1px solid #9aa6bf; border-radius: 6px; }
  #new-note { flex: 1; }
  #filter { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; margin-bottom: 8px; }
  button { padding: 8px 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: #2f6fd0; color: white; }
  ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }
  li { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: white; border: 1px solid #d5dbe8;
       border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; margin: 6px 0; }
  li .text { flex: 1; }
  li.done .text { color: #7a8396; text-decoration: line-through; }
  li.empty { color: #7a8396; justify-content: center; }
  li button { padding: 4px 10px; background: #e3e8f3; color: #1d2433; }
  li button.danger { background: #f6dede; color: #8a1f1f; }
  #status { color: #8a1f1f; min-height: 1.2em; }
</style></head>
<body><main>
  <h1>Notes</h1>
  <form id="add-form">
    <input id="new-note" name="text" required maxlength="200" placeholder="What do you need to remember?"
           aria-label="New note">
    <button id="add">Add</button>
  </form>
  <input id="filter" type="search" placeholder="Filter notes" aria-label="Filter notes">
  <ul id="notes"></ul>
  <p id="summary"></p>
  <p id="status" role="status"></p>
</main></body></html>"""


class NoteStore:
    """Loads and saves the notes list as JSON. A save never leaves a half-written file."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path):
        self.path = path

    def load(self) -> list:
        try:
            data = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return []
        return [{"id": int(n["id"]), "text": str(n["text"]), "done": bool(n["done"])}
                for n in data.get("notes", [])]

    def save(self, notes: list) -> None:
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".notes-", dir=self.path.parent)
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
                json.dump({"version": 1, "notes": notes}, stream, indent=2)
            os.replace(temporary, self.path)
        except BaseException:
            os.unlink(temporary)
            raise


def render_note(note):
    css = "done" if note["done"] else ""
    label = "Undo" if note["done"] else "Done"
    return (f'<li class="{css}" id="note-{note["id"]}">'
            f'<span class="text">{html.escape(note["text"])}</span>'
            f'<button id="done-{note["id"]}">{label}</button>'
            f'<button id="delete-{note["id"]}" class="danger">Delete</button></li>')


def main():
    # Application.start() runs this script twice; everything with side effects comes after it.
    with Application.start(name="Notes") as app:
        path = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path.home() / ".nativehtmlkit-notes.json"
        store = NoteStore(path)
        window = app.open_html(PAGE, title="Notes", width=520, height=640)
        doc = window.document
        try:
            notes = store.load()
        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as error:
            notes = []
            doc.set_text("status", f"Could not read {path.name}: {error}")

        def refresh():
            needle = doc.get_value("filter").strip().casefold()
            shown = [n for n in notes if needle in n["text"].casefold()]
            empty = '<li class="empty">No matching notes.</li>' if notes else '<li class="empty">No notes yet.</li>'
            doc.replace_html("notes", "".join(render_note(n) for n in shown) or empty)
            remaining = sum(1 for n in notes if not n["done"])
            doc.set_text("summary", f"{len(notes)} notes, {remaining} open")

        def save():
            try:
                store.save(notes)
                doc.set_text("status", "")
            except OSError as error:
                doc.set_text("status", f"Not saved: {error.strerror}")

        def add_note(_event):
            text = doc.get_value("new-note").strip()
            if not text:
                return
            next_id = max((n["id"] for n in notes), default=0) + 1
            notes.append({"id": next_id, "text": text, "done": False})
            save()
            refresh()
            doc.set_value("new-note", "")
            doc.focus("new-note")

        def list_clicked(event):
            action, _, note_id = (event.get("element") or "").partition("-")
            note = next((n for n in notes if str(n["id"]) == note_id), None)
            if note is None:
                return
            if action == "done":
                note["done"] = not note["done"]
            elif action == "delete":
                notes.remove(note)
            else:
                return
            save()
            refresh()

        doc.on("submit", add_note, element="add-form")
        doc.on("click", list_clicked, element="notes")
        doc.on("input", lambda _event: refresh(), element="filter")
        refresh()
        doc.focus("new-note")
        app.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
  • NoteStore.save() writes to a temporary file in the same folder and then os.replace()s the real file, so a crash never leaves half a file behind.
  • The file path is the first command-line argument, or .nativehtmlkit-notes.json in your home folder: python notes.py ~/work-notes.json. Arguments survive the re-execution by the host.
  • A read error does not stop the app: it starts empty and shows the reason in #status.
  • doc.on("input", ..., element="filter") fires on every keystroke in the search field; refresh() reads the filter with get_value() and renders only matching notes.
  • #status has role="status", so screen readers announce save errors (Accessibility basics).

  • Use one delegated handler for many buttons, and re-render from a Python model.
  • Persist with an atomic file replace, and take settings from the command line.

items.title: Tutorial: an expense tracker with computed totals (Python UI)
items.text:
You will build Expenses with the nativehtmlkit_ui component library: a form to add expenses, a list of entries, totals per category that update by themselves, and a JSON file that is saved whenever the data changes. You will not write any HTML.

Real capture on KDE Plasma 6.6 Wayland with Core 1.0.3 and Python SDK 0.1.2 + UI 0.1.1.

Time: about 30 minutes. You need: nativehtmlkit_ui installed and the counter from Python UI in five minutes working. Final code: examples/tutorials/python-ui-expenses/expenses.py.

items.title: Step 1: a reactive form
items.text:
examples/tutorials/python-ui-expenses/step1_layout.py
"""Expense tracker tutorial, step 1: a reactive form with nativehtmlkit_ui.

Teaches: state(), two-way inputs (ui.input, ui.select), a text bound to a lambda that re-renders
whenever the states it reads change, cards/rows/columns.
Run:     python step1_layout.py
Guide:   docs/tutorials/python-ui-expenses.md (step 1 of 3)
"""
from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state

CATEGORIES = [("food", "Food"), ("travel", "Travel"), ("home", "Home"), ("other", "Other")]


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Expenses") as app:
        description = state("")
        amount = state("")
        category = state("food")

        ui = UI(title="Expenses", theme="daylight", density="regular", width=640, height=560)
        with ui.column():
            ui.heading("Expenses", level=1)
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("New expense", level=2)
                ui.input(description, label="Description", placeholder="Coffee with Sam")
                with ui.row():
                    ui.input(amount, label="Amount", placeholder="0.00")
                    ui.select(category, CATEGORIES, label="Category")
                ui.text(lambda: f"Preview: {description.value or '(no description)'} - "
                                f"{amount.value or '0'} ({category.value})", muted=True)
        try:
            ui.mount(app)
            app.run()
        finally:
            ui.dispose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Run python step1_layout.py and type into the fields: the preview line follows every keystroke.

  • state("") creates an observable value. ui.input(description, label=...) is two-way: typing updates the state, and setting the state updates the field.
  • ui.select(category, CATEGORIES, ...) takes (value, label) pairs and binds the selected value.
  • ui.text(lambda: ...) binds a text to an expression. The library records which states the lambda reads (description, amount, category) and re-evaluates it when one of them changes.
  • with ui.column():, ui.row() and ui.card() arrange components. The whole tree is built before ui.mount(app); after mounting you change state, not structure.
  • The amount is a plain text field on purpose. A kind="number" field would apply the browser rule step="1", so the host's form validation would reject 12.50. The app validates the amount itself in the next step.

items.title: Step 2: validate and add
items.text:
examples/tutorials/python-ui-expenses/step2_add.py
"""Expense tracker tutorial, step 2: validate input and add expenses to a list.

Teaches: a <form> container with a real submit button (Enter or click both submit), the "submit"
event via ui.on(), validation with Decimal, a bound error message, ui.text_list() with a formatter.
Run:     python step2_add.py
Guide:   docs/tutorials/python-ui-expenses.md (step 2 of 3)
"""
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation

from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state

CATEGORIES = [("food", "Food"), ("travel", "Travel"), ("home", "Home"), ("other", "Other")]
LABELS = dict(CATEGORIES)


def parse_amount(text):
    """Return a positive Decimal with two places, or None."""
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    if not value.is_finite() or value <= 0 or value > Decimal("1000000"):
        return None
    return value.quantize(Decimal("0.01"))


def describe(expense):
    return f"{expense['description']} - {LABELS[expense['category']]} - {expense['amount']}"


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Expenses") as app:
        description = state("")
        amount = state("")
        category = state("food")
        expenses = state([])
        error = state("")

        def add(_event):
            value = parse_amount(amount.value)
            if not description.value.strip():
                error.set("Enter a description.")
            elif value is None:
                error.set("Enter an amount greater than 0, for example 12.50.")
            else:
                entry = {"description": description.value.strip(), "amount": str(value),
                         "category": category.value}
                expenses.set([*expenses.value, entry])  # assign a new list: state is not a deep proxy
                description.set("")
                amount.set("")
                error.set("")

        ui = UI(title="Expenses", theme="daylight", density="regular", width=640, height=620)
        with ui.column():
            ui.heading("Expenses", level=1)
            with ui.card():
                with ui.container("form") as form:
                    ui.input(description, label="Description", placeholder="Coffee with Sam")
                    with ui.row():
                        ui.input(amount, label="Amount", placeholder="0.00")
                        ui.select(category, CATEGORIES, label="Category")
                    ui.element("button", css_class="nhk-button nhk-primary", attrs={"type": "submit"},
                               text="Add expense")
                ui.on(form, "submit", add)
                ui.text(error)
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("This month", level=2)
                ui.text_list(expenses, formatter=describe)
        try:
            ui.mount(app)
            app.run()
        finally:
            ui.dispose()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
  • ui.container("form") puts the fields in a real <form>. ui.element("button", attrs={"type": "submit"}, ...) adds a submit button, so both Enter and a click submit the form, and ui.on(form, "submit", add) receives it. (ui.button() creates type="button" buttons, which never submit a form.)
  • parse_amount() uses Decimal, never float, for money, and accepts only positive amounts.
  • Validation results are state too: error.set(...) shows a message through ui.text(error).
  • expenses.set([*expenses.value, entry]) assigns a new list. State compares values to decide whether anything changed; mutating the existing list in place would not notify anyone.
  • ui.text_list(expenses, formatter=describe) renders one escaped <li> per entry.

items.title: Step 3: totals, actions and saving
items.text:
examples/tutorials/python-ui-expenses/expenses.py
"""Expenses: an expense tracker with computed totals, built with nativehtmlkit_ui (tutorial final code).

Teaches: state() and computed() values, a validated <form> with a submit button, bound text, badges,
lists and conditional regions, buttons that change state, and saving state to a JSON file whenever
it changes (State.subscribe).
Run:     python expenses.py [EXPENSES_FILE]
         (default file: .nativehtmlkit-expenses.json in your home directory)
Guide:   docs/tutorials/python-ui-expenses.md (step 3 of 3)
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
from pathlib import Path

from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, computed, state

CATEGORIES = [("food", "Food"), ("travel", "Travel"), ("home", "Home"), ("other", "Other")]
LABELS = dict(CATEGORIES)


def parse_amount(text):
    """Return a positive Decimal with two places, or None."""
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    if not value.is_finite() or value <= 0 or value > Decimal("1000000"):
        return None
    return value.quantize(Decimal("0.01"))


def describe(expense):
    return f"{expense['description']} - {LABELS.get(expense['category'], 'Other')} - {expense['amount']}"


def load(path):
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    return [{"description": str(e["description"]), "amount": str(parse_amount(str(e["amount"])) or "0.00"),
             "category": e["category"] if e["category"] in LABELS else "other"}
            for e in data.get("expenses", [])]


def save(path, expenses):
    fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".expenses-", dir=path.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            json.dump({"version": 1, "expenses": expenses}, stream, indent=2)
        os.replace(temporary, path)
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(temporary)
        raise


def main():
    with Application.start(name="Expenses") as app:
        path = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path.home() / ".nativehtmlkit-expenses.json"
        description = state("")
        amount = state("")
        category = state("food")
        error = state("")
        try:
            expenses = state(load(path))
        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as problem:
            expenses = state([])
            error.set(f"Could not read {path.name}: {problem}")

        total = computed(lambda: sum((Decimal(e["amount"]) for e in expenses.value), Decimal("0.00")))
        by_category = computed(lambda: [
            f"{label}: {sum((Decimal(e['amount']) for e in expenses.value if e['category'] == key), Decimal('0.00'))}"
            for key, label in CATEGORIES])

        def persist():
            try:
                save(path, expenses.value)
            except OSError as problem:
                error.set(f"Not saved: {problem.strerror}")
        expenses.subscribe(persist)

        def add(_event):
            value = parse_amount(amount.value)
            if not description.value.strip():
                error.set("Enter a description.")
            elif value is None:
                error.set("Enter an amount greater than 0, for example 12.50.")
            else:
                entry = {"description": description.value.strip(), "amount": str(value), "category": category.value}
                expenses.set([*expenses.value, entry])
                description.set("")
                amount.set("")
                error.set("")

        ui = UI(title="Expenses", theme="daylight", density="regular", width=700, height=680)
        with ui.column():
            ui.heading("Expenses", level=1)
            with ui.row():
                ui.badge(lambda: f"Total {total.value}")
                ui.badge(lambda: f"{len(expenses.value)} entries")
            with ui.grid():
                with ui.card():
                    ui.heading("New expense", level=2)
                    with ui.container("form") as form:
                        ui.input(description, label="Description", placeholder="Coffee with Sam")
                        ui.input(amount, label="Amount", placeholder="0.00")
                        ui.select(category, CATEGORIES, label="Category")
                        ui.element("button", css_class="nhk-button nhk-primary", attrs={"type": "submit"},
                                   text="Add expense")
                    ui.on(form, "submit", add)
                    with ui.when(lambda: bool(error.value)):
                        ui.alert(error)
                with ui.card():
                    ui.heading("By category", level=2)
                    ui.text_list(by_category)
            with ui.card():
                ui.heading("Entries", level=2)
                with ui.when(lambda: not expenses.value):
                    ui.text("No expenses yet. Add your first one above.", muted=True)
                ui.text_list(expenses, formatter=describe)
                with ui.row():
                    ui.button("Remove last", variant="secondary",
                              on_click=lambda _e: expenses.set(expenses.value[:-1]))
                    ui.button("Clear all", variant="danger", on_click=lambda _e: expenses.set([]))
        try:
            ui.mount(app)
            app.run()
        finally:
            ui.dispose()
            total.close()
            by_category.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
  • computed(lambda: ...) derives a value from states and recomputes when they change. total and by_category read expenses.value, so adding an entry updates the badge and the category list automatically.
  • with ui.when(lambda: bool(error.value)): shows its contents only while the condition is true. The region stays mounted and is hidden with a CSS class, so inputs inside keep their state.
  • ui.button("Clear all", variant="danger", on_click=...) changes state from a click; the list and totals follow.
  • expenses.subscribe(persist) calls persist() after every change, which writes the file atomically (temporary file, then os.replace). The path is the first command-line argument or .nativehtmlkit-expenses.json in your home folder.
  • In finally, ui.dispose() releases the UI, and each computed is closed.

Threads and computed values

All changes in this app happen in UI event callbacks. If you update states from worker threads, avoid computed() values whose dependencies are changed by several threads at the same time: UI 0.1.1 has a known race there (limitations). See Background work for a safe pattern.
